## create account_collection_flow

<a id="opIdcreateAccountCollectionFlow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/account_collection_flows \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "counterparty_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "payment_types": [
      "string"
    ],
    "receiving_countries": [
      "USA"
    ]
  }'
```

## list bulk_requests

<a id="opIdlistBulkRequests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/bulk_requests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/bulk_requests`

<h3 id="list-bulkrequests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action_type|query|string|false|One of create, or update.|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|resource_type|query|string|false|One of payment_order, expected_payment, or ledger_transaction.|
|status|query|string|false|One of pending, processing, or completed.|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|action_type|create|
|action_type|update|
|action_type|delete|
|resource_type|payment_order|
|resource_type|ledger_account|
|resource_type|ledger_transaction|
|resource_type|expected_payment|
|resource_type|transaction|
|resource_type|transaction_line_item|
|status|pending|
|status|processing|
|status|completed|

<h1 id="modern-treasury-bulkresult">BulkResult</h1>

## list bulk_results

<a id="opIdlistBulkResults"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/bulk_results \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/bulk_results`

<h3 id="list-bulkresults-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|entity_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Unique identifier for the result entity object.|
|entity_type|query|string|false|The type of the request that created this result. bulk_request is the only supported `request_type`|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|request_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Unique identifier for the request that created this bulk result. This is the ID of the bulk request when `request_type` is bulk_request|
|request_type|query|string|false|The type of the request that created this result. bulk_request is the only supported `request_type`|
|status|query|string|false|One of successful or failed.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|entity_type|payment_order|
|entity_type|ledger_account|
|entity_type|ledger_transaction|
|entity_type|expected_payment|
|entity_type|transaction|
|entity_type|transaction_line_item|
|entity_type|bulk_error|
|request_type|bulk_request|
|status|pending|
|status|successful|
|status|failed|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|successful|Inline|

|403|Forbidden|unsuccessful|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|429|Too Many Requests|too many requests|None|

<h3 id="list-bulkresults-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[bulk_result](#schemabulk_result)]|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-After-Cursor|string \| null||The cursor for the next page. Including this in a call as `after_cursor` will return the next page.|
|200|X-Per-Page|integer \| null||The current `per_page`.|

<h1 id="modern-treasury-counterparty">Counterparty</h1>

## list counterparties

<a id="opIdlistCounterparties"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/counterparties \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/counterparties`

Get a paginated list of all counterparties.

<h3 id="list-counterparties-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|created_at_lower_bound|query|string(date-time)|false|Used to return counterparties created after some datetime.|
|created_at_upper_bound|query|string(date-time)|false|Used to return counterparties created before some datetime.|
|email|query|string(email)|false|Performs a partial string match of the email field. This is also case insensitive.|
|external_id|query|string|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|legal_entity_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Filters for counterparties with the given legal entity ID.|
|name|query|string|false|Performs a partial string match of the name field. This is also case insensitive.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

```bash
    },
    "name": "string",
    "send_remittance_advice": true,
    "taxpayer_identifier": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/counterparties/{id}`

Updates a given counterparty with new information.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "external_id": "string",
  "legal_entity_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "send_remittance_advice": true,
  "taxpayer_identifier": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-counterparty-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The id of an existing counterparty.|
|body|body|[counterparty_update_request](#schemacounterparty_update_request)|false|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|false|A new email for the counterparty.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» legal_entity_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|The id of the legal entity.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data in the form of key-value pairs. Pairs can be removed by passing an empty string or `null` as the value.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A new name for the counterparty. Will only update if passed.|
|» send_remittance_advice|body|boolean|false|If this is `true`, Modern Treasury will send an email to the counterparty whenever an associated payment order is sent to the bank.|
|» taxpayer_identifier|body|string|false|Either a valid SSN or EIN.|

## collect account details

<a id="opIdcollectAccountDetails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/counterparties/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/collect_account \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "custom_redirect": "http://example.com",
    "direction": "credit",
    "fields": [
      "name"
    ],
    "send_email": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/counterparties/{id}/collect_account`

Send an email requesting account details.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "custom_redirect": "http://example.com",
  "direction": "credit",
  "fields": [
    "name"
  ],
  "send_email": true
}
```

<h3 id="collect-account-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|counterparty id|
|body|body|[counterparty_collect_account_request](#schemacounterparty_collect_account_request)|false|none|
|» custom_redirect|body|string(uri)|false|The URL you want your customer to visit upon filling out the form. By default, they will be sent to a Modern Treasury landing page. This must be a valid HTTPS URL if set.|
|» direction|body|string|true|One of `credit` or `debit`. Use `credit` when you want to pay a counterparty. Use `debit` when you need to charge a counterparty. This field helps us send a more tailored email to your counterparties."|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|The list of fields you want on the form. This field is optional and if it is not set, will default to [\"nameOnAccount\", \"accountType\", \"accountNumber\", \"routingNumber\", \"address\"]. The full list of options is [\"name\", \"nameOnAccount\", \"taxpayerIdentifier\", \"accountType\", \"accountNumber\", \"routingNumber\", \"address\", \"ibanNumber\", \"swiftCode\"].|
|» send_email|body|boolean|false|By default, Modern Treasury will send an email to your counterparty that includes a link to the form they must fill out. However, if you would like to send the counterparty the link, you can set this parameter to `false`. The JSON body will include the link to the secure Modern Treasury form.|

<h3 id="create-expected-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[expected_payment_create_request](#schemaexpected_payment_create_request)|false|none|
|» amount_lower_bound|body|integer \| null|false|The lowest amount this expected payment may be equal to. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» amount_reconciled|body|integer \| null|false|The amount reconciled for this expected payment. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» amount_reconciled_direction|body|string \| null|false|One of credit or debit. Indicates whether amount_reconciled is a credit or debit amount.|
|» amount_unreconciled|body|integer \| null|false|The amount that remains unreconciled for this expected payment. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» amount_unreconciled_direction|body|string \| null|false|One of credit or debit. Indicates whether amount_unreconciled is a credit or debit amount.|
|» amount_upper_bound|body|integer \| null|false|The highest amount this expected payment may be equal to. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» counterparty_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|The ID of the counterparty you expect for this payment.|
|» currency|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» date_lower_bound|body|string(date) \| null|false|The earliest date the payment may come in. Format: yyyy-mm-dd|
|» date_upper_bound|body|string(date) \| null|false|The latest date the payment may come in. Format: yyyy-mm-dd|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|An optional description for internal use.|
|» direction|body|string \| null|false|One of credit or debit. When you are receiving money, use credit. When you are being charged, use debit.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» internal_account_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|The ID of the Internal Account for the expected payment.|
|» ledger_transaction|body|[ledger_transaction_create_request](#schemaledger_transaction_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger transaction object that will be created with the expected payment. If the ledger transaction cannot be created, then the expected payment creation will fail. The resulting ledger transaction will mirror the status of the expected payment.|
|» ledger_transaction_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Either ledger_transaction or ledger_transaction_id can be provided. Only a pending ledger transaction can be attached upon expected payment creation. Once the expected payment is created, the status of the ledger transaction tracks the expected payment automatically.|
|» line_items|body|[[line_item_request](#schemaline_item_request)]|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» reconciliation_filters|body|object \| null|false|The reconciliation filters you have for this payment.|
|» reconciliation_groups|body|object \| null|false|The reconciliation groups you have for this payment.|
|» reconciliation_rule_variables|body|[[reconciliation_rule_variable](#schemareconciliation_rule_variable)]|false|An array of reconciliation rule variables for this payment.|
|» remittance_information|body|string \| null|false|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string \| null|false|The statement description you expect to see on the transaction. For ACH payments, this will be the full line item passed from the bank. For wire payments, this will be the OBI field on the wire. For check payments, this will be the memo field.|
|» type|body|[expected_payment_type](#schemaexpected_payment_type)|false|One of: ach, au_becs, bacs, book, check, eft, rtp, sepa, wire.|

|» amount_reconciled_direction|debit|

<h3 id="update-expected-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|id|
|body|body|[expected_payment_update_request](#schemaexpected_payment_update_request)|false|none|
|» amount_lower_bound|body|integer \| null|false|The lowest amount this expected payment may be equal to. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» amount_reconciled|body|integer \| null|false|The amount reconciled for this expected payment. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» amount_reconciled_direction|body|string \| null|false|One of credit or debit. Indicates whether amount_reconciled is a credit or debit amount.|
|» amount_unreconciled|body|integer \| null|false|The amount that remains unreconciled for this expected payment. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» amount_unreconciled_direction|body|string \| null|false|One of credit or debit. Indicates whether amount_unreconciled is a credit or debit amount.|
|» amount_upper_bound|body|integer \| null|false|The highest amount this expected payment may be equal to. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» counterparty_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|The ID of the counterparty you expect for this payment.|
|» currency|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» date_lower_bound|body|string(date) \| null|false|The earliest date the payment may come in. Format: yyyy-mm-dd|
|» date_upper_bound|body|string(date) \| null|false|The latest date the payment may come in. Format: yyyy-mm-dd|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|An optional description for internal use.|
|» direction|body|string \| null|false|One of credit or debit. When you are receiving money, use credit. When you are being charged, use debit.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» internal_account_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|The ID of the Internal Account for the expected payment.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» reconciliation_filters|body|object \| null|false|The reconciliation filters you have for this payment.|
|» reconciliation_groups|body|object \| null|false|The reconciliation groups you have for this payment.|
|» reconciliation_rule_variables|body|[[reconciliation_rule_variable](#schemareconciliation_rule_variable)]|false|An array of reconciliation rule variables for this payment.|
|» remittance_information|body|string \| null|false|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string \| null|false|The statement description you expect to see on the transaction. For ACH payments, this will be the full line item passed from the bank. For wire payments, this will be the OBI field on the wire. For check payments, this will be the memo field.|
|» status|body|string \| null|false|The Expected Payment's status can be updated from partially_reconciled to reconciled.|
|» type|body|[expected_payment_type](#schemaexpected_payment_type)|false|One of: ach, au_becs, bacs, book, check, eft, rtp, sepa, wire.|

|Parameter|Value|

|» amount_reconciled_direction|credit|
|» amount_reconciled_direction|debit|
|» amount_unreconciled_direction|credit|
|» amount_unreconciled_direction|debit|
|» direction|credit|
|» direction|debit|
|» status|reconciled|

<h3 id="create-external-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[external_account_create_request](#schemaexternal_account_create_request)|false|none|
|» account_details|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » account_number|body|string|true|none|
|» » account_number_type|body|string|false|none|
|» account_type|body|[external_account_type](#schemaexternal_account_type)|false|Can be `checking`, `savings` or `other`.|
|» contact_details|body|[[contact_detail_create_request](#schemacontact_detail_create_request)]|false|none|
|» counterparty_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» ledger_account|body|[ledger_account_create_request](#schemaledger_account_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger account object that will be created with the external account. The resulting ledger account is linked to the external account for auto-ledgering Payment objects. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/docs/linking-to-other-modern-treasury-objects for more details.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|A nickname for the external account. This is only for internal usage and won't affect any payments|
|» party_address|body|[address_request](#schemaaddress_request)|false|Required if receiving wire payments.|
|» party_identifier|body|string|false|none|
|» party_name|body|string|false|If this value isn't provided, it will be inherited from the counterparty's name.|
|» party_type|body|string \| null|false|Either `individual` or `business`.|
|» plaid_processor_token|body|string|false|If you've enabled the Modern Treasury + Plaid integration in your Plaid account, you can pass the processor token in this field.|
|» routing_details|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » payment_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » routing_number|body|string|true|none|
|» » routing_number_type|body|string|true|none|

## verify external account

<a id="opIdverifyExternalAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/external_accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "currency": "AED",
    "fallback_type": "ach",
    "originating_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "payment_type": "ach",
    "priority": "high"
  }'
```

`POST /api/external_accounts/{id}/verify`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "currency": "AED",
  "fallback_type": "ach",
  "originating_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "payment_type": "ach",
  "priority": "high"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-external-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|external account id|
|body|body|[external_account_verify_request](#schemaexternal_account_verify_request)|false|none|
|» currency|body|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|Defaults to the currency of the originating account.|
|» fallback_type|body|string|false|A payment type to fallback to if the original type is not valid for the receiving account. Currently, this only supports falling back from RTP to ACH (payment_type=rtp and fallback_type=ach)|
|» originating_account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the internal account where the micro-deposits originate from. Both credit and debit capabilities must be enabled.|
|» payment_type|body|string|true|Can be `ach`, `eft`, or `rtp`.|
|» priority|body|string|false|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH transfer. This will apply to both `payment_type` and `fallback_type`.|

<h1 id="modern-treasury-foreignexchangequote">ForeignExchangeQuote</h1>

## list foreign_exchange_quotes

<a id="opIdlistQuotes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/foreign_exchange_quotes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/foreign_exchange_quotes`

<h3 id="list-foreignexchangequotes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|base_currency|query|string|false|Currency to convert, often called the "sell" currency.|
|effective_at_end|query|string(date)|false|An inclusive upper bound for searching effective_at|
|effective_at_start|query|string(date)|false|An inclusive lower bound for searching effective_at|
|expires_at|query|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp until which the quote must be booked by.|
|internal_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|The ID for the `InternalAccount` this quote is associated with.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|target_currency|query|string|false|Currency to convert the `base_currency` to, often called the "buy" currency.|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
  {
    "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",

    "expires_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "foreign_exchange_indicator": "string",
    "foreign_exchange_rate": {
      "base_amount": 0,
      "base_currency": "AED",
      "exponent": 0,
      "rate_string": "string",
      "target_amount": 0,
      "target_currency": "AED",
      "value": 0
    },
    "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "live_mode": true,
    "metadata": {
      "foo": "bar",
      "key": "value",
      "modern": "treasury"
    },
    "object": "string",
    "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "vendor_id": "string"
  }
]
```

```json
    "code": "parameter_invalid",
    "message": "string",
    "parameter": "string"
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|successful|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|bad request|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|401|Unauthorized|unsuccessful|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|403|Forbidden|forbidden|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|429|Too Many Requests|too many requests|None|

<h3 id="list-foreignexchangequotes-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[foreign_exchange_quote](#schemaforeign_exchange_quote)]|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-After-Cursor|string \| null||The cursor for the next page. Including this in a call as `after_cursor` will return the next page.|
|200|X-Per-Page|integer \| null||The current `per_page`.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

## create foreign_exchange_quote

<a id="opIdcreateQuote"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/foreign_exchange_quotes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "base_amount": 0,
    "base_currency": "AED",
    "effective_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "target_amount": 0,
    "target_currency": "AED"
  }'
```

`POST /api/foreign_exchange_quotes`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "base_amount": 0,
  "base_currency": "AED",
  "effective_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "target_amount": 0,
  "target_currency": "AED"
}
```

<h3 id="create-foreignexchangequote-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[foreign_exchange_quote_create_request](#schemaforeign_exchange_quote_create_request)|false|none|
|» base_amount|body|integer|false|Amount in the lowest denomination of the `base_currency` to convert, often called the "sell" amount.|
|» base_currency|body|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|Currency to convert, often called the "sell" currency.|
|» effective_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp until when the quoted rate is valid.|
|» internal_account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID for the `InternalAccount` this quote is associated with.|
|» target_amount|body|integer|false|Amount in the lowest denomination of the `target_currency`, often called the "buy" amount.|
|» target_currency|body|[currency](#schemacurrency)|true|Currency to convert the `base_currency` to, often called the "buy" currency.|

## update identification

<a id="opIdupdateIdentification"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/identifications/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "expiration_date": "1970-01-01",
    "id_number": "string",
    "id_type": "ad_nrt",
    "issuing_country": "string",
    "issuing_region": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/identifications/{id}`

Update an existing Identification.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expiration_date": "1970-01-01",
  "id_number": "string",
  "id_type": "ad_nrt",
  "issuing_country": "string",
  "issuing_region": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-identification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The id of an existing identification.|
|body|body|[identification_update_request](#schemaidentification_update_request)|false|none|
|» expiration_date|body|string(date) \| null|false|The date when the Identification is no longer considered valid by the issuing authority.|
|» id_number|body|string|false|The ID number of identification document.|
|» id_type|body|string|false|The type of ID number.|
|» issuing_country|body|string \| null|false|The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the country that issued the identification|
|» issuing_region|body|string \| null|false|The region in which the identifcation was issued.|

## list incoming payment_details

<a id="opIdlistIncomingPaymentDetails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/incoming_payment_details \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/incoming_payment_details`

Get a list of Incoming Payment Details.

<h3 id="list-incoming-paymentdetails-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|as_of_date_end|query|string(date)|false|Filters incoming payment details with an as_of_date starting on or before the specified date (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|as_of_date_start|query|string(date)|false|Filters incoming payment details with an as_of_date starting on or after the specified date (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|direction|query|string|false|One of `credit` or `debit`.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|status|query|string|false|The current status of the incoming payment order. One of `pending`, `completed`, `returned`, `failed`, or `held`.|
|subtype|query|string|false|An additional layer of classification for the type of incoming payment detail. For example, a `type` of `stablecoin` may have a `subtype` of `ethereum` or `solana`.|
|type|query|string|false|One of: `ach`, `book`, `check`, `eft`, `rtp`, `sepa`, or `wire`.|
|virtual_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|If the incoming payment detail is in a virtual account, the ID of the Virtual Account.|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

|direction|debit|

|type|ach|

|type|eft|
|type|neft|

|type|zengin|

## create async incoming payment detail

<a id="opIdcreateAsyncIncomingPaymentDetail"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/simulations/incoming_payment_details/create_async \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0,
    "as_of_date": "1970-01-01",
    "currency": {},
    "data": {},
    "description": "string",
    "direction": "credit",
    "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "subtype": "string",
    "type": "ach",
    "virtual_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`POST /api/simulations/incoming_payment_details/create_async`

Simulate Incoming Payment Detail

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "as_of_date": "1970-01-01",
  "currency": {},
  "data": {},
  "description": "string",
  "direction": "credit",
  "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "subtype": "string",
  "type": "ach",
  "virtual_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

<h3 id="create-async-incoming-payment-detail-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[incoming_payment_detail_create_request](#schemaincoming_payment_detail_create_request)|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» as_of_date|body|string(date) \| null|false|Defaults to today.|
|» currency|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» data|body|object \| null|false|An object passed through to the simulated IPD that could reflect what a vendor would pass. For `type: check` with `subtype: lockbox` (sandbox Modern Treasury payment accounts only), `data` must include `payor_name`, otherwise the request returns 422.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Defaults to a random description.|
|» direction|body|string|false|One of `credit`, `debit`.|
|» internal_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of one of your internal accounts.|
|» subtype|body|string \| null|false|An additional layer of classification for the type of incoming payment detail, e.g. `ethereum` for a `stablecoin` type. For `type: check`, `subtype: lockbox` simulates a lockbox check deposit.|
|» type|body|string|true|One of `ach`, `wire`, `check`.|
|» virtual_account_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|An optional parameter to associate the incoming payment detail to a virtual account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» direction|credit|
|» direction|debit|
|» type|ach|
|» type|au_becs|
|» type|bacs|
|» type|book|
|» type|check|
|» type|eft|
|» type|neft|
|» type|nz_becs|
|» type|rtp|
|» type|sepa|
|» type|stablecoin|
|» type|wire|
|» type|zengin|

## create internal account

<a id="opIdcreateInternalAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/internal_accounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
```

<h3 id="create-internal-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[internal_account_create_request](#schemainternal_account_create_request)|false|none|
|» account_capabilities|body|[[account_capability](#schemaaccount_capability)]|false|An array of AccountCapability objects that list the originating abilities of the internal account and any relevant information for them.|
|» account_type|body|string|false|The account type, used to provision the appropriate account at the financial institution.|
|» allowed_ach_debit_company_ids|body|[string]|false|The ACH Company IDs allowed to debit this account. `null` allows every company. An empty array allows none. Debits from any other company are returned with code R10. Only applicable to debitable accounts under a Modern Treasury PSP connection.|
|» connection_id|body|string|false|The identifier of the financial institution the account belongs to. If not provided, defaults to the default connection, or the sole connection if only one exists.|
|» counterparty_id|body|string|false|The Counterparty associated to this account.|
|» currency|body|string|true|The currency of the internal account. Supports fiat and stablecoin currencies.|
|» debitable|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether this account can receive ACH debits. Only applicable to accounts created under a Modern Treasury PSP connection, or `null` for Bring Your Own Bank accounts. Defaults to `false`. Configurable only on creation. Please reach out to your customer success manager to enable this capability for your connection.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» legal_entity_id|body|string|false|The LegalEntity associated to this account.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The nickname of the account.|
|» parent_account_id|body|string|false|The parent internal account of this new account.|
|» party_address|body|object|false|The address associated with the owner or null.|
|» » country|body|string|true|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|true|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|true|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|true|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|true|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» party_name|body|string \| null|false|The legal name of the entity which owns the account.|
|» party_type|body|string \| null|false|Either individual or business. Inherits from associated LegalEntity legal_entity_type, if one exists.|
|» requested_account_number_types|body|[string]|false|An array of account number types requested for provisioning.|
|» title|body|string \| null|false|The account title at the financial institution, used in place of the party name. Defaults to the party name if not set. Only applicable to accounts created under supported connections. Please reach out to your customer success manager to enable this capability for your program.|
|» vendor_attributes|body|object|false|A hash of vendor specific attributes that will be used when creating the account at the vendor specified by the given connection.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/invoices \

```

`GET /api/invoices`

<h3 id="list-invoices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|counterparty_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|created_at_end|query|string(date-time)|false|An inclusive upper bound for searching created_at|
|created_at_start|query|string(date-time)|false|An inclusive lower bound for searching created_at|
|due_date_end|query|string(date)|false|An inclusive upper bound for searching due_date|
|due_date_start|query|string(date)|false|An inclusive lower bound for searching due_date|
|expected_payment_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|number|query|string|false|A unique record number assigned to each invoice that is issued.|
|originating_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|payment_order_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|status|query|string|false|none|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

|Parameter|Value|

|status|draft|
|status|paid|

|status|payment_pending|
|status|unpaid|

<h3 id="create-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[invoice_create_request](#schemainvoice_create_request)|false|none|
|» auto_advance|body|boolean \| null|false|When true, the invoice will progress to unpaid automatically and cannot be edited after entering that state. If the invoice fails to progress to unpaid, the errors will be returned and the invoice will not be created.|
|» contact_details|body|[[contact_detail](#schemacontact_detail)]|false|The invoicer's contact details displayed at the top of the invoice.|
|» counterparty_billing_address|body|object \| null|false|The counterparty's billing address.|
|» » country|body|string|true|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|true|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|true|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|true|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|true|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» counterparty_id|body|string|true|The ID of the counterparty receiving the invoice.|
|» counterparty_shipping_address|body|object \| null|false|The counterparty's shipping address where physical goods should be delivered.|
|» » country|body|string|true|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|true|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|true|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|true|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|true|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» currency|body|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|Currency that the invoice is denominated in. Defaults to `USD` if not provided.|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-form description of the invoice.|
|» due_date|body|string(date-time)|true|A future date by when the invoice needs to be paid.|
|» fallback_payment_method|body|string \| null|false|When payment_method is automatic, the fallback payment method to use when an automatic payment fails. One of `manual` or `ui`.|
|» invoice_line_items|body|[[invoice_line_item_create_request](#schemainvoice_line_item_create_request)]|false|An array of invoice line items. The API supports a maximum of 50 invoice line items per invoice. If a greater number of invoice line items is required, please contact support.|
|» invoicer_address|body|object \| null|false|The invoice issuer's business address.|
|» » country|body|string|true|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|true|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|true|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|true|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|true|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» invoicer_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the issuer for the invoice. Defaults to the name of the Organization.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» notification_email_addresses|body|[string]|false|Emails in addition to the counterparty email to send invoice status notifications to. At least one email is required if notifications are enabled and the counterparty doesn't have an email.|
|» notifications_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, the invoice will send email notifications to the invoice recipients about invoice status changes.|
|» originating_account_id|body|string|true|The ID of the internal account the invoice should be paid to.|
|» payment_effective_date|body|string(date)|false|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|» payment_method|body|string|false|The method by which the invoice can be paid. `ui` will show the embedded payment collection flow. `automatic` will automatically initiate payment based upon the account details of the receiving_account id.\nIf the invoice amount is positive, the automatically initiated payment order's direction will be debit. If the invoice amount is negative, the automatically initiated payment order's direction will be credit. One of `manual`, `ui`, or `automatic`.|
|» payment_type|body|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|false|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|» receiving_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The receiving account ID. Can be an `external_account`.|
|» recipient_email|body|string \| null|false|The email of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|» recipient_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|» remind_after_overdue_days|body|[integer]|false|Number of days after due date when overdue reminder emails will be sent out to invoice recipients.|
|» virtual_account_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|The ID of the virtual account the invoice should be paid to.|

|---|---|---|---|

## get invoice

<a id="opIdgetInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/invoices/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/invoices/{id}`

<h3 id="get-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|id|

<h3 id="update-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|id|
|body|body|[invoice_update_request](#schemainvoice_update_request)|false|none|
|» contact_details|body|[[contact_detail](#schemacontact_detail)]|false|The invoicer's contact details displayed at the top of the invoice.|
|» counterparty_billing_address|body|object \| null|false|The counterparty's billing address.|
|» » country|body|string|true|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|true|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|true|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|true|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|true|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» counterparty_id|body|string|false|The ID of the counterparty receiving the invoice.|
|» counterparty_shipping_address|body|object \| null|false|The counterparty's shipping address where physical goods should be delivered.|
|» » country|body|string|true|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|true|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|true|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|true|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|true|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» currency|body|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|Currency that the invoice is denominated in. Defaults to `USD` if not provided.|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-form description of the invoice.|
|» due_date|body|string(date-time)|false|A future date by when the invoice needs to be paid.|
|» fallback_payment_method|body|string \| null|false|When payment_method is automatic, the fallback payment method to use when an automatic payment fails. One of `manual` or `ui`.|
|» invoice_line_items|body|[[invoice_line_item_create_request](#schemainvoice_line_item_create_request)]|false|An array of invoice line items. The API supports a maximum of 50 invoice line items per invoice. If a greater number of invoice line items is required, please contact support.|
|» invoicer_address|body|object \| null|false|The invoice issuer's business address.|
|» » country|body|string|true|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|true|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|true|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|true|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|true|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» invoicer_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the issuer for the invoice. Defaults to the name of the Organization.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» notification_email_addresses|body|[string]|false|Emails in addition to the counterparty email to send invoice status notifications to. At least one email is required if notifications are enabled and the counterparty doesn't have an email.|
|» notifications_enabled|body|boolean|false|If true, the invoice will send email notifications to the invoice recipients about invoice status changes.|
|» originating_account_id|body|string|false|The ID of the internal account the invoice should be paid to.|
|» payment_effective_date|body|string(date)|false|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|» payment_method|body|string|false|The method by which the invoice can be paid. `ui` will show the embedded payment collection flow. `automatic` will automatically initiate payment based upon the account details of the receiving_account id.\nIf the invoice amount is positive, the automatically initiated payment order's direction will be debit. If the invoice amount is negative, the automatically initiated payment order's direction will be credit. One of `manual`, `ui`, or `automatic`.|
|» payment_type|body|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|false|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|» receiving_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The receiving account ID. Can be an `external_account`.|
|» recipient_email|body|string \| null|false|The email of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|» recipient_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|» remind_after_overdue_days|body|[integer]|false|Number of days after due date when overdue reminder emails will be sent out to invoice recipients.|
|» status|body|string|false|Invoice status must be updated in a `PATCH` request that does not modify any other invoice attributes.             Valid state transitions are `draft` to `unpaid`, `draft`, `unpaid` or `paid` to `voided`, and `draft` or             `unpaid` to `paid`.|
|» virtual_account_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|The ID of the virtual account the invoice should be paid to.|

## list payment orders

<a id="opIdlistPaymentOrders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/payment_orders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/payment_orders`

Get a list of all payment orders

<h3 id="list-payment-orders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|counterparty_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|created_at_end|query|string(date)|false|An inclusive upper bound for searching created_at|
|created_at_start|query|string(date)|false|An inclusive lower bound for searching created_at|
|direction|query|string|false|none|
|effective_date_end|query|string(date)|false|An inclusive upper bound for searching effective_date|
|effective_date_start|query|string(date)|false|An inclusive lower bound for searching effective_date|
|external_id|query|string|false|none|
|originating_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|priority|query|string|false|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH and EFT payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH or EFT transfer, respectively. For check payments, `high` can mean an overnight check rather than standard mail.|
|process_after_end|query|string(date-time)|false|An inclusive upper bound for searching process_after|
|process_after_start|query|string(date-time)|false|An inclusive lower bound for searching process_after|
|reference_number|query|string|false|Query for records with the provided reference number|
|status|query|string|false|none|
|transaction_id|query|string(uuid)|false|The ID of a transaction that the payment order has been reconciled to.|
|type|query|string|false|none|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

<h3 id="create-payment-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[payment_order_create_request](#schemapayment_order_create_request)|false|none|
|» accounting|body|[accounting](#schemaaccounting)|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» accounting_category_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting categories. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|» accounting_ledger_class_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting ledger classes. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000 (cents). For RTP, the maximum amount allowed by the network is $10,000,000.|
|» charge_bearer|body|string \| null|false|The party that will pay the fees for the payment order. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/payments/docs/charge-bearer to understand the differences between the options.|
|» currency|body|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|Defaults to the currency of the originating account.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|An optional description for internal use.|
|» direction|body|string|true|One of `credit`, `debit`. Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. A `credit` moves money from your account to someone else's. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own. Note that wire, rtp, and check payments will always be `credit`.|
|» documents|body|[[payment_order_document_create_request](#schemapayment_order_document_create_request)]|false|An array of documents to be attached to the payment order. Note that if you attach documents, the request's content type must be `multipart/form-data`.|
|» effective_date|body|string(date)|false|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|» end_to_end_id|body|string \| null|false|A unique identifier passed through to the receiving bank. Only supported for `ach` (maximum 15 characters) and `wire` (maximum 35 characters). If not provided, Modern Treasury generates one. Some banks may truncate this value or use their own identifier instead.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|RFP payments require an expires_at. This value must be past the effective_date.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» fallback_type|body|string|false|A payment type to fallback to if the original type is not valid for the receiving account. Currently, this only supports falling back from RTP to ACH (type=rtp and fallback_type=ach)|
|» foreign_exchange_contract|body|string \| null|false|If present, indicates a specific foreign exchange contract number that has been generated by your financial institution.|
|» foreign_exchange_indicator|body|string \| null|false|Indicates the type of FX transfer to initiate, can be either `variable_to_fixed`, `fixed_to_variable`, or `null` if the payment order currency matches the originating account currency.|
|» ledger_transaction|body|[ledger_transaction_create_request](#schemaledger_transaction_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger transaction object that will be created with the payment order. If the ledger transaction cannot be created, then the payment order creation will fail. The resulting ledger transaction will mirror the status of the payment order.|
|» ledger_transaction_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Either ledger_transaction or ledger_transaction_id can be provided. Only a pending ledger transaction can be attached upon payment order creation. Once the payment order is created, the status of the ledger transaction tracks the payment order automatically.|
|» line_items|body|[[line_item_request](#schemaline_item_request)]|false|An array of line items that must sum up to the amount of the payment order.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» nsf_protected|body|boolean|false|A boolean to determine if NSF Protection is enabled for this payment order. Note that this setting must also be turned on in your organization settings page.|
|» originating_account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of one of your organization's internal accounts.|
|» originating_party_address|body|object \| null|false|If present, this address will override the default originating party address used on the payment order. This works across all payment types.|
|» » country|body|string \| null|false|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » line2|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string \| null|false|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string \| null|false|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string \| null|false|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» originating_party_name|body|string \| null|false|If present, this will replace your default company name on receiver's bank statement. This field can only be used for ACH payments currently. For ACH, only the first 16 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|» originating_secondary_party_name|body|string \| null|false|Secondary name for the legal entity making the payment.  Can be used for e.g. check signatures where the originating party wishes to retain their company's display name but use an employee's name for the signature.|
|» priority|body|string|false|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH and EFT payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH or EFT transfer, respectively. For check payments, `high` can mean an overnight check rather than standard mail.|
|» process_after|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|If present, Modern Treasury will not process the payment until after this time. If `process_after` is past the cutoff for `effective_date`, `process_after` will take precedence and `effective_date` will automatically update to reflect the earliest possible sending date after `process_after`. Format is ISO8601 timestamp.|
|» purpose|body|string \| null|false|For `wire`, this is usually the purpose which is transmitted via the "InstrForDbtrAgt" field in the ISO20022 file. For `eft`, this field is the 3 digit CPA Code that will be attached to the payment.|
|» receiving_account|body|object|false|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|» » account_details|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » account_number|body|string|true|none|
|» » » account_number_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » account_type|body|[external_account_type](#schemaexternal_account_type)|false|Can be `checking`, `savings` or `other`.|
|» » contact_details|body|[[contact_detail_create_request](#schemacontact_detail_create_request)]|false|none|
|» » external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» » ledger_account|body|[ledger_account_create_request](#schemaledger_account_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger account object that will be created with the external account. The resulting ledger account is linked to the external account for auto-ledgering Payment objects. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/docs/linking-to-other-modern-treasury-objects for more details.|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|A nickname for the external account. This is only for internal usage and won't affect any payments|
|» » party_address|body|[address_request](#schemaaddress_request)|false|Required if receiving wire payments.|
|» » party_identifier|body|string|false|none|
|» » party_name|body|string|false|If this value isn't provided, it will be inherited from the counterparty's name.|
|» » party_type|body|string \| null|false|Either `individual` or `business`.|
|» » plaid_processor_token|body|string|false|If you've enabled the Modern Treasury + Plaid integration in your Plaid account, you can pass the processor token in this field.|
|» » routing_details|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » payment_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » » routing_number|body|string|true|none|
|» » » routing_number_type|body|string|true|none|
|» receiving_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|» reconciliation_status|body|string|false|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|» remittance_information|body|string \| null|false|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|» send_remittance_advice|body|boolean \| null|false|Send an email to the counterparty when the payment order is sent to the bank. If `null`, `send_remittance_advice` on the Counterparty is used.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string \| null|false|An optional descriptor which will appear in the receiver's statement. For `check` payments this field will be used as the memo line. For `ach` the maximum length is 10 characters. Note that for ACH payments, the name on your bank account will be included automatically by the bank, so you can use the characters for other useful information. For `eft` the maximum length is 15 characters.|
|» subtype|body|[payment_order_subtype](#schemapayment_order_subtype)|false|An additional layer of classification for the type of payment order you are doing. This field is only used for `ach` payment orders currently. For `ach`  payment orders, the `subtype`  represents the SEC code. We currently support `CCD`, `PPD`, `IAT`, `CTX`, `WEB`, `CIE`, and `TEL`.|
|» transaction_monitoring_enabled|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** A flag that determines whether a payment order should go through transaction monitoring.|
|» type|body|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|true|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|» ultimate_originating_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ultimate originating account ID. Can be a `virtual_account` or `internal_account`.|
|» ultimate_originating_party_address|body|object \| null|false|Address of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|» » country|body|string|false|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|false|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|false|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|false|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|false|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» ultimate_originating_party_identifier|body|string \| null|false|Identifier of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|» ultimate_originating_party_name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|» ultimate_receiving_party_identifier|body|string \| null|false|Identifier of the ultimate funds recipient.|
|» ultimate_receiving_party_name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the ultimate funds recipient.|
|» vendor_attributes|body|object|false|Additional vendor specific fields for this payment. Data must be represented as key-value pairs.|

<h3 id="create-payment-order-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|successful|[payment_order](#schemapayment_order)|
|400|Bad Request|parameter_invalid|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|401|Unauthorized|unsuccessful|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|403|Forbidden|forbidden|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|409|Conflict|conflict|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|unsuccessful|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|unsuccessful|[error_message](#schemaerror_message)|
|429|Too Many Requests|too many requests|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic_auth
</aside>

<h3 id="create-async-payment-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[payment_order_async_create_request](#schemapayment_order_async_create_request)|false|none|
|» accounting|body|[accounting](#schemaaccounting)|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» accounting_category_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting categories. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|» accounting_ledger_class_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting ledger classes. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|» amount|body|integer|true|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000 (cents). For RTP, the maximum amount allowed by the network is $10,000,000.|
|» charge_bearer|body|string \| null|false|The party that will pay the fees for the payment order. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/payments/docs/charge-bearer to understand the differences between the options.|
|» currency|body|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|Defaults to the currency of the originating account.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|An optional description for internal use.|
|» direction|body|string|true|One of `credit`, `debit`. Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. A `credit` moves money from your account to someone else's. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own. Note that wire, rtp, and check payments will always be `credit`.|
|» effective_date|body|string(date)|false|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|» end_to_end_id|body|string \| null|false|A unique identifier passed through to the receiving bank. Only supported for `ach` (maximum 15 characters) and `wire` (maximum 35 characters). If not provided, Modern Treasury generates one. Some banks may truncate this value or use their own identifier instead.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|RFP payments require an expires_at. This value must be past the effective_date.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» fallback_type|body|string|false|A payment type to fallback to if the original type is not valid for the receiving account. Currently, this only supports falling back from RTP to ACH (type=rtp and fallback_type=ach)|
|» foreign_exchange_contract|body|string \| null|false|If present, indicates a specific foreign exchange contract number that has been generated by your financial institution.|
|» foreign_exchange_indicator|body|string \| null|false|Indicates the type of FX transfer to initiate, can be either `variable_to_fixed`, `fixed_to_variable`, or `null` if the payment order currency matches the originating account currency.|
|» ledger_transaction|body|[ledger_transaction_create_request](#schemaledger_transaction_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger transaction object that will be created with the payment order. If the ledger transaction cannot be created, then the payment order creation will fail. The resulting ledger transaction will mirror the status of the payment order.|
|» ledger_transaction_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Either ledger_transaction or ledger_transaction_id can be provided. Only a pending ledger transaction can be attached upon payment order creation. Once the payment order is created, the status of the ledger transaction tracks the payment order automatically.|
|» line_items|body|[[line_item_request](#schemaline_item_request)]|false|An array of line items that must sum up to the amount of the payment order.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» nsf_protected|body|boolean|false|A boolean to determine if NSF Protection is enabled for this payment order. Note that this setting must also be turned on in your organization settings page.|
|» originating_account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of one of your organization's internal accounts.|
|» originating_party_address|body|object \| null|false|If present, this address will override the default originating party address used on the payment order. This works across all payment types.|
|» » country|body|string \| null|false|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » line2|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string \| null|false|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string \| null|false|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string \| null|false|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» originating_party_name|body|string \| null|false|If present, this will replace your default company name on receiver's bank statement. This field can only be used for ACH payments currently. For ACH, only the first 16 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|» originating_secondary_party_name|body|string \| null|false|Secondary name for the legal entity making the payment.  Can be used for e.g. check signatures where the originating party wishes to retain their company's display name but use an employee's name for the signature.|
|» priority|body|string|false|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH and EFT payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH or EFT transfer, respectively. For check payments, `high` can mean an overnight check rather than standard mail.|
|» process_after|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|If present, Modern Treasury will not process the payment until after this time. If `process_after` is past the cutoff for `effective_date`, `process_after` will take precedence and `effective_date` will automatically update to reflect the earliest possible sending date after `process_after`. Format is ISO8601 timestamp.|
|» purpose|body|string \| null|false|For `wire`, this is usually the purpose which is transmitted via the "InstrForDbtrAgt" field in the ISO20022 file. For `eft`, this field is the 3 digit CPA Code that will be attached to the payment.|
|» receiving_account|body|object|false|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|» » account_details|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » account_number|body|string|true|none|
|» » » account_number_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » account_type|body|[external_account_type](#schemaexternal_account_type)|false|Can be `checking`, `savings` or `other`.|
|» » contact_details|body|[[contact_detail_create_request](#schemacontact_detail_create_request)]|false|none|
|» » external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» » ledger_account|body|[ledger_account_create_request](#schemaledger_account_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger account object that will be created with the external account. The resulting ledger account is linked to the external account for auto-ledgering Payment objects. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/docs/linking-to-other-modern-treasury-objects for more details.|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|A nickname for the external account. This is only for internal usage and won't affect any payments|
|» » party_address|body|[address_request](#schemaaddress_request)|false|Required if receiving wire payments.|
|» » party_identifier|body|string|false|none|
|» » party_name|body|string|false|If this value isn't provided, it will be inherited from the counterparty's name.|
|» » party_type|body|string \| null|false|Either `individual` or `business`.|
|» » plaid_processor_token|body|string|false|If you've enabled the Modern Treasury + Plaid integration in your Plaid account, you can pass the processor token in this field.|
|» » routing_details|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » payment_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » » routing_number|body|string|true|none|
|» » » routing_number_type|body|string|true|none|
|» receiving_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|» reconciliation_status|body|string|false|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|» remittance_information|body|string \| null|false|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|» send_remittance_advice|body|boolean \| null|false|Send an email to the counterparty when the payment order is sent to the bank. If `null`, `send_remittance_advice` on the Counterparty is used.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string \| null|false|An optional descriptor which will appear in the receiver's statement. For `check` payments this field will be used as the memo line. For `ach` the maximum length is 10 characters. Note that for ACH payments, the name on your bank account will be included automatically by the bank, so you can use the characters for other useful information. For `eft` the maximum length is 15 characters.|
|» subtype|body|[payment_order_subtype](#schemapayment_order_subtype)|false|An additional layer of classification for the type of payment order you are doing. This field is only used for `ach` payment orders currently. For `ach`  payment orders, the `subtype`  represents the SEC code. We currently support `CCD`, `PPD`, `IAT`, `CTX`, `WEB`, `CIE`, and `TEL`.|
|» transaction_monitoring_enabled|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** A flag that determines whether a payment order should go through transaction monitoring.|
|» type|body|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|true|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|» ultimate_originating_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ultimate originating account ID. Can be a `virtual_account` or `internal_account`.|
|» ultimate_originating_party_address|body|object \| null|false|Address of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|» » country|body|string|false|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string|false|none|
|» » line2|body|string|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string|false|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string|false|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string|false|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» ultimate_originating_party_identifier|body|string \| null|false|Identifier of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|» ultimate_originating_party_name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|» ultimate_receiving_party_identifier|body|string \| null|false|Identifier of the ultimate funds recipient.|
|» ultimate_receiving_party_name|body|string \| null|false|Name of the ultimate funds recipient.|
|» vendor_attributes|body|object|false|Additional vendor specific fields for this payment. Data must be represented as key-value pairs.|
