<h3 id="update-payment-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[payment_order_update_request](#schemapayment_order_update_request)|false|none|
|» accounting|body|[accounting](#schemaaccounting)|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» accounting_category_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting categories. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|» accounting_ledger_class_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting ledger classes. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000 (cents). For RTP, the maximum amount allowed by the network is $10,000,000.|
|» charge_bearer|body|string \| null|false|The party that will pay the fees for the payment order. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/payments/docs/charge-bearer to understand the differences between the options.|
|» counterparty_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|Required when receiving_account_id is passed the ID of an external account.|
|» currency|body|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|Defaults to the currency of the originating account.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|An optional description for internal use.|
|» direction|body|string|false|One of `credit`, `debit`. Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. A `credit` moves money from your account to someone else's. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own. Note that wire, rtp, and check payments will always be `credit`.|
|» effective_date|body|string(date)|false|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|» end_to_end_id|body|string \| null|false|A unique identifier passed through to the receiving bank. Only supported for `ach` (maximum 15 characters) and `wire` (maximum 35 characters). If not provided, Modern Treasury generates one. Some banks may truncate this value or use their own identifier instead.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|RFP payments require an expires_at. This value must be past the effective_date.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» fallback_type|body|string|false|A payment type to fallback to if the original type is not valid for the receiving account. Currently, this only supports falling back from RTP to ACH (type=rtp and fallback_type=ach)|
|» foreign_exchange_contract|body|string \| null|false|If present, indicates a specific foreign exchange contract number that has been generated by your financial institution.|
|» foreign_exchange_indicator|body|string \| null|false|Indicates the type of FX transfer to initiate, can be either `variable_to_fixed`, `fixed_to_variable`, or `null` if the payment order currency matches the originating account currency.|
|» line_items|body|[[line_item_request](#schemaline_item_request)]|false|An array of line items that must sum up to the amount of the payment order.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» nsf_protected|body|boolean|false|A boolean to determine if NSF Protection is enabled for this payment order. Note that this setting must also be turned on in your organization settings page.|
|» originating_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of one of your organization's internal accounts.|
|» originating_party_address|body|object \| null|false|If present, this address will override the default originating party address used on the payment order. This works across all payment types.|
|» » country|body|string \| null|false|Country code conforms to [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2]|
|» » line1|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » line2|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » locality|body|string \| null|false|Locality or City. Use the full city name rather than an abbreviation (e.g. San Francisco).|
|» » postal_code|body|string \| null|false|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string \| null|false|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|
|» originating_party_name|body|string \| null|false|If present, this will replace your default company name on receiver's bank statement. This field can only be used for ACH payments currently. For ACH, only the first 16 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|» originating_secondary_party_name|body|string \| null|false|Secondary name for the legal entity making the payment.  Can be used for e.g. check signatures where the originating party wishes to retain their company's display name but use an employee's name for the signature.|
|» priority|body|string|false|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH and EFT payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH or EFT transfer, respectively. For check payments, `high` can mean an overnight check rather than standard mail.|
|» process_after|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|If present, Modern Treasury will not process the payment until after this time. If `process_after` is past the cutoff for `effective_date`, `process_after` will take precedence and `effective_date` will automatically update to reflect the earliest possible sending date after `process_after`. Format is ISO8601 timestamp.|
|» purpose|body|string \| null|false|For `wire`, this is usually the purpose which is transmitted via the "InstrForDbtrAgt" field in the ISO20022 file. For `eft`, this field is the 3 digit CPA Code that will be attached to the payment.|
|» receiving_account|body|object|false|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|» » account_details|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » account_number|body|string|true|none|
|» » » account_number_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » account_type|body|[external_account_type](#schemaexternal_account_type)|false|Can be `checking`, `savings` or `other`.|
|» » contact_details|body|[[contact_detail_create_request](#schemacontact_detail_create_request)]|false|none|
|» » external_id|body|string \| null|false|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|» » ledger_account|body|[ledger_account_create_request](#schemaledger_account_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger account object that will be created with the external account. The resulting ledger account is linked to the external account for auto-ledgering Payment objects. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/docs/linking-to-other-modern-treasury-objects for more details.|
|» » metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|A nickname for the external account. This is only for internal usage and won't affect any payments|
|» » party_address|body|[address_request](#schemaaddress_request)|false|Required if receiving wire payments.|
|» » party_identifier|body|string|false|none|
|» » party_name|body|string|false|If this value isn't provided, it will be inherited from the counterparty's name.|
|» » party_type|body|string \| null|false|Either `individual` or `business`.|
|» » plaid_processor_token|body|string|false|If you've enabled the Modern Treasury + Plaid integration in your Plaid account, you can pass the processor token in this field.|
|» » routing_details|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » payment_type|body|string|false|none|
|» » » routing_number|body|string|true|none|
|» » » routing_number_type|body|string|true|none|
|» receiving_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|» reconciliation_status|body|string|false|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|» remittance_information|body|string \| null|false|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|» send_remittance_advice|body|boolean \| null|false|Send an email to the counterparty when the payment order is sent to the bank. If `null`, `send_remittance_advice` on the Counterparty is used.|
|» statement_descriptor|body|string \| null|false|An optional descriptor which will appear in the receiver's statement. For `check` payments this field will be used as the memo line. For `ach` the maximum length is 10 characters. Note that for ACH payments, the name on your bank account will be included automatically by the bank, so you can use the characters for other useful information. For `eft` the maximum length is 15 characters.|
|» status|body|string|false|To cancel a payment order, use `cancelled`. To redraft a returned payment order, use `approved`. To undo approval on a denied or approved payment order, use `needs_approval`.|
|» subtype|body|[payment_order_subtype](#schemapayment_order_subtype)|false|An additional layer of classification for the type of payment order you are doing. This field is only used for `ach` payment orders currently. For `ach`  payment orders, the `subtype`  represents the SEC code. We currently support `CCD`, `PPD`, `IAT`, `CTX`, `WEB`, `CIE`, and `TEL`.|
|» type|body|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|false|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|» ultimate_originating_party_identifier|body|string \| null|false|This represents the identifier by which the person is known to the receiver when using the CIE subtype for ACH payments. Only the first 22 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|» ultimate_originating_party_name|body|string \| null|false|This represents the name of the person that the payment is on behalf of when using the CIE subtype for ACH payments. Only the first 15 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|» ultimate_receiving_party_identifier|body|string \| null|false|This represents the name of the merchant that the payment is being sent to when using the CIE subtype for ACH payments. Only the first 22 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|» ultimate_receiving_party_name|body|string \| null|false|This represents the identifier by which the merchant is known to the person initiating an ACH payment with CIE subtype. Only the first 15 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|

## create invoice_line_item

<a id="opIdcreateInvoiceLineItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/invoices/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/invoice_line_items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "direction": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "foo": "bar",
      "key": "value",
      "modern": "treasury"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "quantity": 0,
    "unit_amount": 0,
    "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/invoices/{invoice_id}/invoice_line_items`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "direction": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "quantity": 0,
  "unit_amount": 0,
  "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-invoicelineitem-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|invoice_id|path|string(uuid)|true|invoice_id|
|body|body|[invoice_line_item_create_request](#schemainvoice_line_item_create_request)|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional free-form description of the line item.|
|» direction|body|string|false|Either `debit` or `credit`. `debit` indicates that a client owes the business money           and increases the invoice's `total_amount` due. `credit` has the opposite intention and effect.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the line item, typically a product or SKU name.|
|» quantity|body|integer|false|The number of units of a product or service that this line item is for.           Must be a whole number. Defaults to 1 if not provided.|
|» unit_amount|body|integer|true|The cost per unit of the product or service that this line item is for,           specified in the invoice currency's smallest unit.|
|» unit_amount_decimal|body|string|false|The cost per unit of the product or service that this line item is for,           specified in the invoice currency's smallest unit. Accepts decimal strings with up to 12 decimals|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "description": "string",
```

## update invoice_line_item

<a id="opIdupdateInvoiceLineItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/invoices/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/invoice_line_items/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "direction": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "foo": "bar",
      "key": "value",
      "modern": "treasury"
    },
    "name": "string",
    "quantity": 0,
    "unit_amount": 0,
    "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/invoices/{invoice_id}/invoice_line_items/{id}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "direction": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "name": "string",
  "quantity": 0,
  "unit_amount": 0,
  "unit_amount_decimal": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-invoicelineitem-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|id|
|invoice_id|path|string(uuid)|true|invoice_id|
|body|body|[invoice_line_item_update_request](#schemainvoice_line_item_update_request)|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional free-form description of the line item.|
|» direction|body|string|false|Either `debit` or `credit`. `debit` indicates that a client owes the business money           and increases the invoice's `total_amount` due. `credit` has the opposite intention and effect.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the line item, typically a product or SKU name.|
|» quantity|body|integer|false|The number of units of a product or service that this line item is for.           Must be a whole number. Defaults to 1 if not provided.|
|» unit_amount|body|integer|false|The cost per unit of the product or service that this line item is for,           specified in the invoice currency's smallest unit.|
|» unit_amount_decimal|body|string|false|The cost per unit of the product or service that this line item is for,           specified in the invoice currency's smallest unit. Accepts decimal strings with up to 12 decimals|

`GET /api/ledger_account_categories`

Get a list of ledger account categories.

<h3 id="list-ledgeraccountcategories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|balances|query|object|false|For example, if you want the balances as of a particular time (ISO8601), the encoded query string would be `balances%5Beffective_at%5D=2000-12-31T12:00:00Z`. The balances as of a time are inclusive of entries with that exact time, but with respect to the ledger accounts that are currently present in the category.|
|currency|query|string|false|none|
|external_id|query|string|false|none|
|ledger_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Query categories which contain a ledger account directly or through child categories.|
|ledger_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|name|query|string|false|none|
|parent_ledger_account_category_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Query categories that are nested underneath a parent category|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|id[]|query|[string]|false|If you have specific IDs to retrieve in bulk, you can pass them as query parameters delimited with `id[]=`, for example `?id[]=123&id[]=abc`.|
|name[]|query|[string]|false|If you have specific names to retrieve in bulk, you can pass them as query parameters delimited with `name[]=`, for example `?name[]=123&name[]=abc`.|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/ledger_account_settlements \
```

```bash
  -d '{
    "allow_either_direction": true,
    "contra_ledger_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "description": "string",
    "effective_at_upper_bound": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "metadata": {
      "foo": "bar",
      "key": "value",
      "modern": "treasury"
    },
    "settled_ledger_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "skip_settlement_ledger_transaction": true,
    "status": "pending"
  }'
```

`POST /api/ledger_account_settlements`

Create a ledger account settlement.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_either_direction": true,
  "contra_ledger_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "description": "string",
  "effective_at_upper_bound": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "settled_ledger_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "skip_settlement_ledger_transaction": true,
  "status": "pending"
}
```

<h3 id="create-ledgeraccountsettlement-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[ledger_account_settlement_create_request](#schemaledger_account_settlement_create_request)|false|none|
|» allow_either_direction|body|boolean \| null|false|If true, the settlement amount and settlement_entry_direction will bring the settlement ledger account's balance closer to zero, even if the balance is negative.|
|» contra_ledger_account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The id of the contra ledger account that sends to or receives funds from the settled ledger account.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|The description of the ledger account settlement.|
|» effective_at_upper_bound|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The exclusive upper bound of the effective_at timestamp of the ledger entries to be included in the ledger account settlement. The default value is the created_at timestamp of the ledger account settlement.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» settled_ledger_account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The id of the settled ledger account whose ledger entries are queried against, and its balance is reduced as a result.|
|» skip_settlement_ledger_transaction|body|boolean \| null|false|It is set to `false` by default. It should be set to `true` when migrating existing settlements.|
|» status|body|string \| null|false|The status of the ledger account settlement. It is set to `pending` by default. To post a ledger account settlement at creation, use `posted`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|pending|
|» status|posted|
|» status|drafting|

<h3 id="list-ledgeraccounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|available_balance_amount|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), `eq` (=), or `not_eq` (!=) to filter by balance amount.|
|balances|query|object|false|Use `balances[effective_at_lower_bound]` and `balances[effective_at_upper_bound]` to get the balances change between the two timestamps. The lower bound is inclusive while the upper bound is exclusive of the provided timestamps. If no value is supplied the balances will be retrieved not including that bound.|
|created_at|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by the created at timestamp. For example, for all times after Jan 1 2000 12:00 UTC, use created_at%5Bgt%5D=2000-01-01T12:00:00Z.|
|currency|query|string|false|none|
|external_id|query|string|false|none|
|ledger_account_category_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledger_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|normal_balance|query|string|false|none|
|pending_balance_amount|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), `eq` (=), or `not_eq` (!=) to filter by balance amount.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|posted_balance_amount|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), `eq` (=), or `not_eq` (!=) to filter by balance amount.|
|updated_at|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by the updated at timestamp. For example, for all times after Jan 1 2000 12:00 UTC, use updated_at%5Bgt%5D=2000-01-01T12:00:00Z.|
|id[]|query|[string]|false|If you have specific IDs to retrieve in bulk, you can pass them as query parameters delimited with `id[]=`, for example `?id[]=123&id[]=abc`.|
|name[]|query|[string]|false|If you have specific names to retrieve in bulk, you can pass them as query parameters delimited with `name[]=`, for example `?name[]=123&name[]=abc`.|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

<h1 id="modern-treasury-ledgerentry">LedgerEntry</h1>

## list ledger_entries

<a id="opIdlistLedgerEntries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/ledger_entries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /api/ledger_entries`

Get a list of all ledger entries.

<h3 id="list-ledgerentries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|amount|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by amount.|
|as_of_lock_version|query|integer|false|Shows all ledger entries that were present on a ledger account at a particular `lock_version`. You must also specify `ledger_account_id`.|
|direction|query|string|false|If true, response will include ledger entries that were deleted. When you update a ledger transaction to specify a new set of entries, the previous entries are deleted.|
|effective_at|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by the transaction's effective time. Format ISO8601|
|effective_date|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by the transaction's effective date. Format YYYY-MM-DD|
|ledger_account_category_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Get all ledger entries that match the direction specified. One of `credit`, `debit`.|
|ledger_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledger_account_lock_version|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by the lock_version of a ledger account. For example, for all entries created at or before before lock_version 1000 of a ledger account, use `ledger_account_lock_version%5Blte%5D=1000`.|
|ledger_account_payout_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledger_account_settlement_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledger_account_statement_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Get all ledger entries that are included in the ledger account statement.|
|ledger_transaction_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|order_by|query|object|false|Order by `created_at` or `effective_at` in `asc` or `desc` order. For example, to order by `effective_at asc`, use `order_by%5Beffective_at%5D=asc`. Ordering by only one field at a time is supported.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|show_balances|query|boolean|false|If true, response will include the balances attached to the ledger entry. If there is no balance available, null will be returned instead.|
|show_deleted|query|boolean|false|If true, response will include ledger entries that were deleted. When you update a ledger transaction to specify a new set of entries, the previous entries are deleted.|
|status|query|string|false|Get all ledger entries that match the status specified. One of `pending`, `posted`, or `archived`. For multiple statuses, use `status[]=pending&status[]=posted`.|
|status[]|query|[string]|false|Get all ledger entries that match the status specified. One of `pending`, `posted`, or `archived`. For multiple statuses, use `status[]=pending&status[]=posted`.|
|updated_at|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by the posted at timestamp. For example, for all times after Jan 1 2000 12:00 UTC, use updated_at%5Bgt%5D=2000-01-01T12:00:00Z.|
|id[]|query|[string]|false|If you have specific IDs to retrieve in bulk, you can pass them as query parameters delimited with `id[]=`, for example `?id[]=123&id[]=abc`.|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|credit|
|direction|debit|
|status|pending|
|status|posted|
|status|archived|
|status[]|pending|
|status[]|posted|
|status[]|archived|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "amount": 0,
    "amount_string": "string",
```

`GET /api/ledger_transactions`

Get a list of ledger transactions.

<h3 id="list-ledgertransactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|amount|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by amount.|
|effective_at|query|object|false|Use "gt" (>), "gte" (>=), "lt" (<), "lte" (<=), or "eq" (=) to filter by effective at. For example, for all transactions after Jan 1 2000, use effective_at%5Bgt%5D=2000-01-01T00:00:00:00.000Z.|
|effective_date|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by effective date. For example, for all dates after Jan 1 2000, use effective_date%5Bgt%5D=2000-01-01.|
|external_id|query|string|false|none|
|ledger_account_category_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledger_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledger_account_settlement_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledger_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledgerable_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|ledgerable_type|query|string|false|none|
|order_by|query|object|false|Order by `created_at` or `effective_at` in `asc` or `desc` order. For example, to order by `effective_at asc`, use `order_by%5Beffective_at%5D=asc`. Ordering by only one field at a time is supported.|
|partially_posts_ledger_transaction_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|posted_at|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by the posted at timestamp. For example, for all times after Jan 1 2000 12:00 UTC, use posted_at%5Bgt%5D=2000-01-01T12:00:00Z.|
|reverses_ledger_transaction_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|status|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|updated_at|query|object|false|Use `gt` (>), `gte` (>=), `lt` (<), `lte` (<=), or `eq` (=) to filter by the posted at timestamp. For example, for all times after Jan 1 2000 12:00 UTC, use updated_at%5Bgt%5D=2000-01-01T12:00:00Z.|
|id[]|query|[string]|false|If you have specific IDs to retrieve in bulk, you can pass them as query parameters delimited with `id[]=`, for example `?id[]=123&id[]=abc`.|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

<h3 id="create-ledgertransaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[ledger_transaction_create_request](#schemaledger_transaction_create_request)|false|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|An optional description for internal use.|
|» effective_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp (ISO8601 format) at which the ledger transaction happened for reporting purposes.|
|» effective_date|body|string(date)|false|The date (YYYY-MM-DD) on which the ledger transaction happened for reporting purposes.|
|» external_id|body|string|false|A unique string to represent the ledger transaction. Only one pending or posted ledger transaction may have this ID in the ledger.|
|» ledger_entries|body|[[ledger_entry_create_request](#schemaledger_entry_create_request)]|true|An array of ledger entry objects.|
|» ledgerable_id|body|string(uuid)|false|If the ledger transaction can be reconciled to another object in Modern Treasury, the id will be populated here, otherwise null.|
|» ledgerable_type|body|string|false|If the ledger transaction can be reconciled to another object in Modern Treasury, the type will be populated here, otherwise null. This can be one of payment_order, incoming_payment_detail, expected_payment, return, or reversal.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» status|body|string|false|To post a ledger transaction at creation, use `posted`.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ledgerable_type|expected_payment|
|» ledgerable_type|incoming_payment_detail|
|» ledgerable_type|payment_order|
|» ledgerable_type|return|
|» ledgerable_type|reversal|
|» status|archived|
|» status|pending|
|» status|posted|

`POST /api/ledger_transactions/{id}/reversal`

Create a ledger transaction reversal.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "effective_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "external_id": "string",
  "ledgerable_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "ledgerable_type": "expected_payment",
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "status": "archived"
}
```

<h3 id="create-ledgertransaction-reversal-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The id of ledger transaction to reverse.|
|body|body|[ledger_transaction_reversal_create_request](#schemaledger_transaction_reversal_create_request)|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional free-form description for the reversal ledger transaction. Maximum of 1000 characters allowed.|
|» effective_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|The timestamp (ISO8601 format) at which the reversal ledger transaction happened for reporting purposes. It defaults to the `effective_at` of the original ledger transaction if not provided.|
|» external_id|body|string|false|Must be unique within the ledger.|
|» ledgerable_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Specify this if you'd like to link the reversal ledger transaction to a Payment object like Return or Reversal.|
|» ledgerable_type|body|string|false|Specify this if you'd like to link the reversal ledger transaction to a Payment object like Return or Reversal.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data to be added to the reversal ledger transaction as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» status|body|string|false|Status of the reversal ledger transaction. It defaults to `posted` if not provided.|

|» ledgerable_type|incoming_payment_detail|
|» ledgerable_type|payment_order|

|» status|archived|
|» status|pending|
|» status|posted|

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[legal_entity_create_request](#schemalegal_entity_create_request)|false|none|
|» addresses|body|[[legal_entity_address_create_request](#schemalegal_entity_address_create_request)]|false|A list of addresses for the entity.|
|» bank_settings|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » backup_withholding_percentage|body|integer \| null|true|The percentage of backup withholding to apply to the legal entity.|
|» » created_at|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» » discarded_at|body|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|
|» » enable_backup_withholding|body|boolean \| null|true|Whether backup withholding is enabled. See more here - https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/backup-withholding.|
|» » id|body|string(uuid)|true|none|
|» » live_mode|body|boolean|true|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|» » object|body|string|true|none|
|» » privacy_opt_out|body|boolean \| null|true|Cross River Bank specific setting to opt out of privacy policy.|
|» » regulation_o|body|boolean \| null|true|It covers, among other types of insider loans, extensions of credit by a member bank to an executive officer, director, or principal shareholder of the member bank; a bank holding company of which the member bank is a subsidiary; and any other subsidiary of that bank holding company.|
|» » updated_at|body|string(date-time)|true|none|
|» business_description|body|string \| null|false|A description of the business.|
|» business_designation|body|string \| null|false|Legal designation associated with the business.|
|» business_name|body|string \| null|false|The business's legal business name.|
|» citizenship_country|body|string \| null|false|The country of citizenship for an individual.|
|» compliance_details|body|object \| null|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» connection_id|body|string \| null|false|The connection ID for the connection the legal entity is associated with. Defaults to the id of the connection designated with an is_default value of true or the id of an existing operational connection if only one is available. Pass in a value of null to prevent the connection from being associated with the legal entity.|
|» country_of_incorporation|body|string \| null|false|The country where the business is incorporated, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. US).|
|» date_formed|body|string(date) \| null|false|A business's formation date (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|» date_of_birth|body|string(date) \| null|false|An individual's date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|» documents|body|[object]|false|A list of documents to attach to the legal entity (e.g. articles of incorporation, certificate of good standing, proof of address).|

|» first_name|body|string \| null|false|An individual's first name.|
|» identifications|body|[[identification_create_request](#schemaidentification_create_request)]|false|A list of identifications for the legal entity.|
|» industry_classifications|body|[[legal_entity_industry_classification](#schemalegal_entity_industry_classification)]|false|A list of industry classifications for the legal entity.|

## update legal entity status

<a id="opIdupdateLegalEntityStatus"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/simulations/legal_entities/string/update_status \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "status": "active"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/simulations/legal_entities/{id}/update_status`

Update Legal Entity Status (sandbox only)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "status": "active"
}
```

<h3 id="update-legal-entity-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Legal entity ID|
|body|body|[legal_entity_update_status_request](#schemalegal_entity_update_status_request)|false|none|
|» status|body|string|true|The target status for the legal entity. One of `active`, `suspended`, or `denied`. Valid transitions depend on the current status.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|suspended|
|» status|denied|

|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|status|query|string|false|Filter by payment actions of a specific status.|
|type|query|string|false|The type of payment action.|

<h3 id="create-return-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[return_create_request](#schemareturn_create_request)|false|none|
|» additional_information|body|string \| null|false|Some returns may include additional information from the bank. In these cases, this string will be present.|
|» code|body|string \| null|false|The return code. For ACH returns, this is the required ACH return code.|
|» corrections|body|object \| null|false|Only relevant for ACH NOC returns. This is an object containing all of the new and corrected information provided by the bank that was previously incorrect on the original outgoing payment.|
|» » account_number|body|string \| null|false|The updated account number that should replace the one originally used on the outgoing payment.|
|» » company_id|body|string \| null|false|The updated company ID that should replace the one originally used on the outgoing payment.|
|» » company_name|body|string \| null|false|The updated company name that should replace the one originally used on the outgoing payment.|
|» » individual_identification_number|body|string \| null|false|The updated individual identification number that should replace the one originally used on the outgoing payment.|
|» » routing_number|body|string \| null|false|The updated routing number that should replace the one originally used on the outgoing payment.|
|» » transaction_code|body|string \| null|false|The updated account type code that should replace the one originally used on the outgoing payment.|
|» data|body|object \| null|false|The raw data from the return file that we get from the bank.|
|» date_of_death|body|string(date) \| null|false|If the return code is `R14` or `R15` this is the date the deceased counterparty passed away.|
|» ledger_transaction|body|[ledger_transaction_create_request](#schemaledger_transaction_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger transaction object that will be created with the return. If the ledger transaction cannot be created, then the return creation will fail. The resulting ledger transaction will mirror the status of the return.|
|» reason|body|string \| null|false|An optional description of the reason for the return. This is for internal usage and will not be transmitted to the bank.”|
|» reconciliation_status|body|string|false|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|» returnable_id|body|string(uuid) \| null|true|The ID of the object being returned or `null`.|
|» returnable_type|body|string|true|The type of object being returned. Currently, this may only be incoming_payment_detail.|

`GET /api/transactions`

Get a list of all transactions.

<h3 id="list-transactions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after_cursor|query|string \| null|false|none|
|as_of_date_end|query|string(date)|false|Filters transactions with an `as_of_date` starting on or before the specified date (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|as_of_date_start|query|string(date)|false|Filters transactions with an `as_of_date` starting on or after the specified date (YYYY-MM-DD).|
|counterparty_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|description|query|string|false|Filters for transactions including the queried string in the description.|
|direction|query|string|false|none|
|internal_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Specify `internal_account_id` if you wish to see transactions to/from a specific account.|
|payment_type|query|string|false|none|
|per_page|query|integer|false|none|
|posted|query|boolean|false|Either `true` or `false`.|
|vendor_id|query|string|false|Filters for transactions including the queried vendor id (an identifier given to transactions by the bank).|
|virtual_account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|none|
|metadata|query|object|false|For example, if you want to query for records with metadata key `Type` and value `Loan`, the query would be `metadata%5BType%5D=Loan`. This encodes the query parameters.|

## create transaction

<a id="opIdcreateTransaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/transactions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0,
    "amount_string": "string",
    "as_of_date": "1970-01-01",
    "direction": "string",
    "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "metadata": {
      "foo": "bar",
      "key": "value",
      "modern": "treasury"
    },
    "posted": true,
    "type": "ach",
    "vendor_code": "string",
    "vendor_code_type": "string",
    "vendor_customer_id": "string",
    "vendor_description": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/transactions`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "amount_string": "string",
  "as_of_date": "1970-01-01",
  "direction": "string",
  "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "posted": true,
  "type": "ach",
  "vendor_code": "string",
  "vendor_code_type": "string",
  "vendor_customer_id": "string",
  "vendor_description": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[transaction_create_request](#schematransaction_create_request)|false|none|
|» amount|body|integer|false|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|» amount_string|body|string|false|The transaction amount as a string, preserving full precision for values that may exceed safe integer limits in some languages.|
|» as_of_date|body|string(date) \| null|true|The date on which the transaction occurred.|
|» direction|body|string|true|Either `credit` or `debit`.|
|» internal_account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the relevant Internal Account.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» posted|body|boolean|false|This field will be `true` if the transaction has posted to the account.|
|» type|body|string \| null|false|The type of the transaction. Examples could be `card, `ach`, `wire`, `check`, `rtp`, or `book`.|
|» vendor_code|body|string \| null|true|When applicable, the bank-given code that determines the transaction's category. For most banks this is the BAI2/BTRS transaction code.|
|» vendor_code_type|body|string \| null|true|The type of `vendor_code` being reported. Can be one of `bai2`, `bankprov`, `bnk_dev`, `cleartouch`, `currencycloud`, `cross_river`, `dwolla`, `evolve`, `goldman_sachs`, `iso20022`, `jpmc`, `mx`, `silvergate`, `swift`, `us_bank`, or others.|
|» vendor_customer_id|body|string \| null|false|An identifier given to this transaction by the bank, often `null`.|
|» vendor_description|body|string \| null|false|The transaction detail text that often appears in on your bank statement and in your banking portal.|

|» type|sepa|

|» type|stablecoin|
|» type|wire|
|» type|zengin|
|» type|other|

<h3 id="create-virtualaccount-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|This key should be something unique, preferably something like an UUID.|
|body|body|[virtual_account_create_request](#schemavirtual_account_create_request)|false|none|
|» account_details|body|[[account_detail_create_request](#schemaaccount_detail_create_request)]|false|An array of account detail objects.|
|» counterparty_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the counterparty that the virtual account belongs to.|
|» credit_ledger_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of a credit normal ledger account. When money leaves the virtual account, this ledger account will be credited. Must be accompanied by a debit_ledger_account_id if present.|
|» debit_ledger_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of a debit normal ledger account. When money enters the virtual account, this ledger account will be debited. Must be accompanied by a credit_ledger_account_id if present.|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional description for internal use.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|A user-defined identifier for the virtual account.|
|» internal_account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the internal account that this virtual account is associated with.|
|» ledger_account|body|[ledger_account_create_request](#schemaledger_account_create_request)|false|Specifies a ledger account object that will be created with the virtual account. The resulting ledger account is linked to the virtual account for auto-ledgering IPDs.|
|» ledger_account_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ledger account that you'd like to link to the virtual account.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the virtual account.|
|» party_address|body|[address_request](#schemaaddress_request)|false|The address of the owner of the virtual account. When absent, the internal account's party address is used.|
|» routing_details|body|[[routing_detail_create_request](#schemarouting_detail_create_request)]|false|An array of routing detail objects.|
|» virtual_account_setting_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the virtual account setting used to allocate this virtual account.|

|» » postal_code|body|string \| null|false|The postal code of the address.|
|» » region|body|string \| null|false|Region or State. This field is free-form; for US states, we recommend a two-letter code (e.g. CA). Full state names are also accepted.|

## update line item

<a id="opIdupdateLineItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://app.moderntreasury.com/api/expected_payments/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/line_items/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "metadata": {
      "foo": "bar",
      "key": "value",
      "modern": "treasury"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/{itemizable_type}/{itemizable_id}/line_items/{id}`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-line-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the line item.|
|itemizable_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the payment order or expected payment.|
|itemizable_type|path|string|true|One of `payment_orders` or `expected_payments`.|
|body|body|[line_item_update_request](#schemaline_item_update_request)|false|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

|itemizable_type|payment_orders|

```json
  ],

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|custom_redirect|string(uri)|false|none|The URL you want your customer to visit upon filling out the form. By default, they will be sent to a Modern Treasury landing page. This must be a valid HTTPS URL if set.|
|direction|string|true|none|One of `credit` or `debit`. Use `credit` when you want to pay a counterparty. Use `debit` when you need to charge a counterparty. This field helps us send a more tailored email to your counterparties."|
|fields|[string]|false|none|The list of fields you want on the form. This field is optional and if it is not set, will default to [\"nameOnAccount\", \"accountType\", \"accountNumber\", \"routingNumber\", \"address\"]. The full list of options is [\"name\", \"nameOnAccount\", \"taxpayerIdentifier\", \"accountType\", \"accountNumber\", \"routingNumber\", \"address\", \"ibanNumber\", \"swiftCode\"].|
|send_email|boolean|false|none|By default, Modern Treasury will send an email to your counterparty that includes a link to the form they must fill out. However, if you would like to send the counterparty the link, you can set this parameter to `false`. The JSON body will include the link to the secure Modern Treasury form.|

|fallback_type|string|false|none|A payment type to fallback to if the original type is not valid for the receiving account. Currently, this only supports falling back from RTP to ACH (payment_type=rtp and fallback_type=ach)|
|originating_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of the internal account where the micro-deposits originate from. Both credit and debit capabilities must be enabled.|
|payment_type|string|true|none|Can be `ach`, `eft`, or `rtp`.|
|priority|string|false|none|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH transfer. This will apply to both `payment_type` and `fallback_type`.|

<h2 id="tocS_foreign_exchange_quote">foreign_exchange_quote</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaforeign_exchange_quote"></a>
<a id="schema_foreign_exchange_quote"></a>
<a id="tocSforeign_exchange_quote"></a>
<a id="tocsforeign_exchange_quote"></a>

```json
{
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "effective_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "expires_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "foreign_exchange_indicator": "string",
  "foreign_exchange_rate": {
    "base_amount": 0,
    "base_currency": "AED",
    "exponent": 0,
    "rate_string": "string",
    "target_amount": 0,
    "target_currency": "AED",
    "value": 0
  },
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "live_mode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "object": "string",
  "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "vendor_id": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|effective_at|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp until when the quoted rate is valid.|
|expires_at|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp until which the quote must be booked by.|
|foreign_exchange_indicator|string|true|none|Either `fixed_to_variable` if the `base_amount` was specified, or `variable_to_fixed` if the `target_amount` was specified when requesting the quote.|
|foreign_exchange_rate|[foreign_exchange_rate](#schemaforeign_exchange_rate)|true|none|The serialized rate information represented by this quote.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|internal_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID for the `InternalAccount` this quote is associated with.|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|vendor_id|string|false|none|This vendor assigned ID for this quote.|

```json
  "base_amount": 0,
  "base_currency": "AED",
  "exponent": 0,
  "rate_string": "string",
  "target_amount": 0,
  "target_currency": "AED",
  "value": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|base_amount|integer|true|none|Amount in the lowest denomination of the `base_currency` to convert, often called the "sell" amount.|
|base_currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|true|none|Currency to convert, often called the "sell" currency.|
|exponent|integer|true|none|The exponent component of the rate. The decimal is calculated as `value` / (10 ^ `exponent`).|
|rate_string|string|true|none|A string representation of the rate.|
|target_amount|integer|true|none|Amount in the lowest denomination of the `target_currency`, often called the "buy" amount.|
|target_currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|true|none|Currency to convert the `base_currency` to, often called the "buy" currency.|
|value|integer|true|none|The whole number component of the rate. The decimal is calculated as `value` / (10 ^ `exponent`).|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|as_of_date|string(date)|true|none|The date on which the corresponding transaction will occur.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|true|none|The currency of the incoming payment detail.|
|data|object|true|none|The raw data from the payment pre-notification file that we get from the bank.|
|direction|string|true|none|One of `credit` or `debit`.|
|failure_reason|string \| null|true|none|The reason the incoming payment detail failed, or `null`.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|internal_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of the Internal Account for the incoming payment detail. This is always present.|
|ledger_transaction_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The ID of the ledger transaction linked to the incoming payment detail or `null`.|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|originating_account_number|string \| null|false|none|The account number of the originating account for the incoming payment detail.|
|originating_account_number_safe|string \| null|true|none|The last 4 digits of the originating account_number for the incoming payment detail.|
|originating_account_number_type|string \| null|true|none|The type of the originating account number for the incoming payment detail.|
|originating_party_address|object \| null|false|none|The address of the originating party for the incoming payment detail, or `null`.|
|originating_party_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the originating party for the incoming payment detail.|
|originating_party_vendor_identifier|string \| null|false|none|The vendor-assigned identifier for the originating party of the incoming payment detail, or `null`.|
|originating_routing_number|string \| null|true|none|The routing number of the originating account for the incoming payment detail.|
|originating_routing_number_type|string \| null|true|none|The type of the originating routing number for the incoming payment detail.|
|receiving_account_number|string \| null|false|none|The account number of the receiving account for the incoming payment detail, or `null`.|
|receiving_account_number_safe|string \| null|false|none|The last 4 digits of the receiving account number for the incoming payment detail, or `null`.|
|reconciliation_status|string|true|none|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|status|string|true|none|The current status of the incoming payment order. One of `pending`, `completed`, `returned`, `failed`, or `held`.|
|subtype|string \| null|true|none|An additional layer of classification for the type of incoming payment detail. For example, a `type` of `stablecoin` may have a `subtype` of `ethereum` or `solana`.|
|transaction_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The ID of the reconciled Transaction or `null`.|
|transaction_line_item_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The ID of the reconciled Transaction Line Item or `null`.|
|type|string|true|none|One of: `ach`, `book`, `check`, `eft`, `rtp`, `sepa`, or `wire`.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|vendor_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The identifier of the vendor bank.|
|virtual_account|object \| null|true|none|If the incoming payment detail is in a virtual account, the serialized virtual account object.|
|virtual_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|If the incoming payment detail is in a virtual account, the ID of the Virtual Account.|

<h2 id="tocS_incoming_payment_detail_create_request">incoming_payment_detail_create_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaincoming_payment_detail_create_request"></a>
<a id="schema_incoming_payment_detail_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocSincoming_payment_detail_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocsincoming_payment_detail_create_request"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "as_of_date": "1970-01-01",
  "currency": {},
  "data": {},
  "description": "string",
  "direction": "credit",
  "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "subtype": "string",
  "type": "ach",
  "virtual_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|false|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|as_of_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|Defaults to today.|
|currency|string \| null|false|none|none|
|data|object \| null|false|none|An object passed through to the simulated IPD that could reflect what a vendor would pass. For `type: check` with `subtype: lockbox` (sandbox Modern Treasury payment accounts only), `data` must include `payor_name`, otherwise the request returns 422.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Defaults to a random description.|
|direction|string|false|none|One of `credit`, `debit`.|
|internal_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ID of one of your internal accounts.|
|subtype|string \| null|false|none|An additional layer of classification for the type of incoming payment detail, e.g. `ethereum` for a `stablecoin` type. For `type: check`, `subtype: lockbox` simulates a lockbox check deposit.|
|type|string|true|none|One of `ach`, `wire`, `check`.|
|virtual_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|An optional parameter to associate the incoming payment detail to a virtual account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|credit|
|direction|debit|
|type|ach|
|type|au_becs|
|type|bacs|
|type|book|
|type|check|
|type|eft|
|type|neft|
|type|nz_becs|
|type|rtp|
|type|sepa|
|type|stablecoin|
|type|wire|
|type|zengin|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_capabilities|[[account_capability](#schemaaccount_capability)]|true|none|An array of AccountCapability objects that list the originating abilities of the internal account and any relevant information for them.|
|account_details|[[account_detail](#schemaaccount_detail)]|true|none|An array of account detail objects.|
|account_type|string \| null|true|none|Can be checking, savings or other.|
|allowed_ach_debit_company_ids|[string]|true|none|The ACH Company IDs allowed to debit this account. `null` allows every company. An empty array allows none. Debits from any other company are returned with code R10. Only applicable to debitable accounts under a Modern Treasury PSP connection.|
|connection|[connection](#schemaconnection)|true|none|Specifies which financial institution the accounts belong to.|
|contra_ledger_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|If the internal account links to a contra ledger account in Modern Treasury, the id of the contra ledger account will be populated here.|
|counterparty_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The Counterparty associated to this account.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|true|none|The currency of the account.|
|debitable|boolean \| null|true|none|Whether this account can receive ACH debits. Only applicable to accounts created under a Modern Treasury PSP connection, or `null` for Bring Your Own Bank accounts. Defaults to `false`. Configurable only on creation. Please reach out to your customer success manager to enable this capability for your connection.|
|external_id|string \| null|true|none|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|ledger_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|If the internal account links to a ledger account in Modern Treasury, the id of the ledger account will be populated here.|
|legal_entity_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The Legal Entity associated to this account.|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|name|string \| null|true|none|A nickname for the account.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|parent_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The parent InternalAccount of this account.|
|party_address|[address](#schemaaddress)|true|none|The address associated with the owner or null.|
|party_name|string|true|none|The legal name of the entity which owns the account.|
|party_type|string \| null|true|none|Either individual or business. Inherits from associated LegalEntity legal_entity_type, if one exists.|
|routing_details|[[routing_detail](#schemarouting_detail)]|true|none|An array of routing detail objects.|
|status|string(string) \| null|true|none|The internal account status.|
|title|string|true|none|The account title at the financial institution. Defaults to the party name unless a custom title was set on creation. Custom titles are only applicable to accounts created under supported connections.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|vendor_id|string(string) \| null|true|none|The vendor ID associated with this account.|

```json
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_capabilities|[[account_capability](#schemaaccount_capability)]|false|none|An array of AccountCapability objects that list the originating abilities of the internal account and any relevant information for them.|
|account_type|string|false|none|The account type, used to provision the appropriate account at the financial institution.|
|allowed_ach_debit_company_ids|[string]|false|none|The ACH Company IDs allowed to debit this account. `null` allows every company. An empty array allows none. Debits from any other company are returned with code R10. Only applicable to debitable accounts under a Modern Treasury PSP connection.|
|connection_id|string|false|none|The identifier of the financial institution the account belongs to. If not provided, defaults to the default connection, or the sole connection if only one exists.|
|counterparty_id|string|false|none|The Counterparty associated to this account.|
|currency|string|true|none|The currency of the internal account. Supports fiat and stablecoin currencies.|
|debitable|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether this account can receive ACH debits. Only applicable to accounts created under a Modern Treasury PSP connection, or `null` for Bring Your Own Bank accounts. Defaults to `false`. Configurable only on creation. Please reach out to your customer success manager to enable this capability for your connection.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|legal_entity_id|string|false|none|The LegalEntity associated to this account.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|name|string|true|none|The nickname of the account.|
|parent_account_id|string|false|none|The parent internal account of this new account.|
|party_address|object|false|none|The address associated with the owner or null.|
|party_name|string \| null|false|none|The legal name of the entity which owns the account.|
|party_type|string \| null|false|none|Either individual or business. Inherits from associated LegalEntity legal_entity_type, if one exists.|
|requested_account_number_types|[string]|false|none|An array of account number types requested for provisioning.|
|title|string \| null|false|none|The account title at the financial institution, used in place of the party name. Defaults to the party name if not set. Only applicable to accounts created under supported connections. Please reach out to your customer success manager to enable this capability for your program.|
|vendor_attributes|object|false|none|A hash of vendor specific attributes that will be used when creating the account at the vendor specified by the given connection.|

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowed_ach_debit_company_ids|[string]|false|none|The ACH Company IDs allowed to debit this account. `null` allows every company. An empty array allows none. Debits from any other company are returned with code R10. Only applicable to debitable accounts under a Modern Treasury PSP connection.|

|ledger_account_id|string|false|none|The Ledger Account associated to this account.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Additional data in the form of key-value pairs. Pairs can be removed by passing an empty string or `null` as the value.|

|parent_account_id|string|false|none|The parent internal account for this account.|
|party_address|object \| null|false|none|The address associated with the owner of the internal account. Updating this value does not guarantee that the new address matches the address on record with the account's bank; you are responsible for verifying that the address is accurate.|

|amount_paid|integer|true|none|Amount paid on the invoice in specified currency's smallest unit, e.g., $10 USD would be represented as 1000.|
|amount_remaining|integer|true|none|Amount remaining due on the invoice in specified currency's smallest unit, e.g., $10 USD would be represented as 1000.|
|contact_details|[[contact_detail](#schemacontact_detail)]|true|none|The invoicer's contact details displayed at the top of the invoice.|
|counterparty_billing_address|object \| null|true|none|The counterparty's billing address.|
|counterparty_id|string|true|none|The ID of the counterparty receiving the invoice.|
|counterparty_shipping_address|object \| null|true|none|The counterparty's shipping address where physical goods should be delivered.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|true|none|Currency that the invoice is denominated in. Defaults to `USD` if not provided.|
|description|string|true|none|An optional free-form description of the invoice.|
|due_date|string(date-time)|true|none|A future date by when the invoice needs to be paid.|
|expected_payments|[[expected_payment](#schemaexpected_payment)]|true|none|The expected payments created for an unpaid invoice.|
|fallback_payment_method|string \| null|true|none|When payment_method is automatic, the fallback payment method to use when an automatic payment fails. One of `manual` or `ui`.|
|hosted_url|string|true|none|The URL of the hosted web UI where the invoice can be viewed.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|invoicer_address|object \| null|true|none|The invoice issuer's business address.|
|invoicer_name|string \| null|true|none|The name of the issuer for the invoice. Defaults to the name of the Organization.|
|issued_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|The time at which the invoice was issued.|
|ledger_account_settlement_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|**Deprecated.** The ledger account settlement object linked to the invoice.|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|metadata|object \| null|true|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|notification_email_addresses|[string]|true|none|Emails in addition to the counterparty email to send invoice status notifications to. At least one email is required if notifications are enabled and the counterparty doesn't have an email.|
|notifications_enabled|boolean|true|none|If true, the invoice will send email notifications to the invoice recipients about invoice status changes.|
|number|string|true|none|A unique record number assigned to each invoice that is issued.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|originating_account_id|string|true|none|The ID of the internal account the invoice should be paid to.|
|paid_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|The time at which the invoice was paid.|
|payment_effective_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|payment_method|string \| null|true|none|When opening an invoice, whether to show the embedded payment UI , automatically debit the recipient, or rely on manual payment from the recipient.|
|payment_orders|[[payment_order](#schemapayment_order)]|true|none|The payment orders created for paying the invoice through the invoice payment UI.|
|payment_type|string \| null|true|none|One of `ach` or `eft`.|
|pdf_url|string \| null|true|none|The URL where the invoice PDF can be downloaded.|
|receiving_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The receiving account ID. Can be an `internal_account`.|
|recipient_email|string \| null|true|none|The email of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|recipient_name|string \| null|true|none|The name of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|remind_after_overdue_days|[integer]|true|none|Number of days after due date when overdue reminder emails will be sent out to invoice recipients.|
|status|string|true|none|The status of the invoice.|
|total_amount|integer|true|none|Total amount due in specified currency's smallest unit, e.g., $10 USD would be represented as 1000.|
|transaction_line_item_ids|[string(uuid)]|true|none|IDs of transaction line items associated with an invoice.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|virtual_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The ID of the virtual account the invoice should be paid to.|
|voided_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|The time at which the invoice was voided.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auto_advance|boolean \| null|false|none|When true, the invoice will progress to unpaid automatically and cannot be edited after entering that state. If the invoice fails to progress to unpaid, the errors will be returned and the invoice will not be created.|
|contact_details|[[contact_detail](#schemacontact_detail)]|false|none|The invoicer's contact details displayed at the top of the invoice.|
|counterparty_billing_address|object \| null|false|none|The counterparty's billing address.|
|counterparty_id|string|true|none|The ID of the counterparty receiving the invoice.|
|counterparty_shipping_address|object \| null|false|none|The counterparty's shipping address where physical goods should be delivered.|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|none|Currency that the invoice is denominated in. Defaults to `USD` if not provided.|
|description|string|false|none|A free-form description of the invoice.|
|due_date|string(date-time)|true|none|A future date by when the invoice needs to be paid.|
|fallback_payment_method|string \| null|false|none|When payment_method is automatic, the fallback payment method to use when an automatic payment fails. One of `manual` or `ui`.|
|invoice_line_items|[[invoice_line_item_create_request](#schemainvoice_line_item_create_request)]|false|none|An array of invoice line items. The API supports a maximum of 50 invoice line items per invoice. If a greater number of invoice line items is required, please contact support.|
|invoicer_address|object \| null|false|none|The invoice issuer's business address.|
|invoicer_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the issuer for the invoice. Defaults to the name of the Organization.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|notification_email_addresses|[string]|false|none|Emails in addition to the counterparty email to send invoice status notifications to. At least one email is required if notifications are enabled and the counterparty doesn't have an email.|
|notifications_enabled|boolean|false|none|If true, the invoice will send email notifications to the invoice recipients about invoice status changes.|
|originating_account_id|string|true|none|The ID of the internal account the invoice should be paid to.|
|payment_effective_date|string(date)|false|none|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|payment_method|string|false|none|The method by which the invoice can be paid. `ui` will show the embedded payment collection flow. `automatic` will automatically initiate payment based upon the account details of the receiving_account id.\nIf the invoice amount is positive, the automatically initiated payment order's direction will be debit. If the invoice amount is negative, the automatically initiated payment order's direction will be credit. One of `manual`, `ui`, or `automatic`.|
|payment_type|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|false|none|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|receiving_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The receiving account ID. Can be an `external_account`.|
|recipient_email|string \| null|false|none|The email of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|recipient_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|remind_after_overdue_days|[integer]|false|none|Number of days after due date when overdue reminder emails will be sent out to invoice recipients.|
|virtual_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|The ID of the virtual account the invoice should be paid to.|

```json
  },
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|The total amount for this line item specified in the invoice currency's smallest unit.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|description|string|true|none|An optional free-form description of the line item.|
|direction|string|true|none|Either `debit` or `credit`. `debit` indicates that a client owes the business money           and increases the invoice's `total_amount` due. `credit` has the opposite intention and effect.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|invoice_id|string|true|none|The ID of the invoice for this line item.|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the line item, typically a product or SKU name.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|quantity|integer|true|none|The number of units of a product or service that this line item is for.           Must be a whole number. Defaults to 1 if not provided.|
|unit_amount|integer|true|none|The cost per unit of the product or service that this line item is for,           specified in the invoice currency's smallest unit.|
|unit_amount_decimal|string|true|none|The cost per unit of the product or service that this line item is for,           specified in the invoice currency's smallest unit. Accepts decimal strings with up to 12 decimals|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

|unit_amount_decimal|string|false|none|The cost per unit of the product or service that this line item is for,           specified in the invoice currency's smallest unit. Accepts decimal strings with up to 12 decimals|
