### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|contact_details|[[contact_detail](#schemacontact_detail)]|false|none|The invoicer's contact details displayed at the top of the invoice.|
|counterparty_billing_address|object \| null|false|none|The counterparty's billing address.|
|counterparty_id|string|false|none|The ID of the counterparty receiving the invoice.|
|counterparty_shipping_address|object \| null|false|none|The counterparty's shipping address where physical goods should be delivered.|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|none|Currency that the invoice is denominated in. Defaults to `USD` if not provided.|
|description|string|false|none|A free-form description of the invoice.|
|due_date|string(date-time)|false|none|A future date by when the invoice needs to be paid.|
|fallback_payment_method|string \| null|false|none|When payment_method is automatic, the fallback payment method to use when an automatic payment fails. One of `manual` or `ui`.|
|invoice_line_items|[[invoice_line_item_create_request](#schemainvoice_line_item_create_request)]|false|none|An array of invoice line items. The API supports a maximum of 50 invoice line items per invoice. If a greater number of invoice line items is required, please contact support.|
|invoicer_address|object \| null|false|none|The invoice issuer's business address.|
|invoicer_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the issuer for the invoice. Defaults to the name of the Organization.|
|metadata|object \| null|false|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|notification_email_addresses|[string]|false|none|Emails in addition to the counterparty email to send invoice status notifications to. At least one email is required if notifications are enabled and the counterparty doesn't have an email.|
|notifications_enabled|boolean|false|none|If true, the invoice will send email notifications to the invoice recipients about invoice status changes.|
|originating_account_id|string|false|none|The ID of the internal account the invoice should be paid to.|
|payment_effective_date|string(date)|false|none|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|payment_method|string|false|none|The method by which the invoice can be paid. `ui` will show the embedded payment collection flow. `automatic` will automatically initiate payment based upon the account details of the receiving_account id.\nIf the invoice amount is positive, the automatically initiated payment order's direction will be debit. If the invoice amount is negative, the automatically initiated payment order's direction will be credit. One of `manual`, `ui`, or `automatic`.|
|payment_type|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|false|none|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|receiving_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The receiving account ID. Can be an `external_account`.|
|recipient_email|string \| null|false|none|The email of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|recipient_name|string \| null|false|none|The name of the recipient of the invoice. Leaving this value as null will fallback to using the counterparty's name.|
|remind_after_overdue_days|[integer]|false|none|Number of days after due date when overdue reminder emails will be sent out to invoice recipients.|
|status|string|false|none|Invoice status must be updated in a `PATCH` request that does not modify any other invoice attributes.             Valid state transitions are `draft` to `unpaid`, `draft`, `unpaid` or `paid` to `voided`, and `draft` or             `unpaid` to `paid`.|
|virtual_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|The ID of the virtual account the invoice should be paid to.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000. Can be any integer up to 36 digits.|
|amount_string|string|true|none|The amount of the ledger entry as a string, preserving full precision for values that may exceed safe integer limits in some languages.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|direction|string|true|none|One of `credit`, `debit`. Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. A `credit` moves money from your account to someone else's. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own. Note that wire, rtp, and check payments will always be `credit`.|
|discarded_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|none|
|effective_at|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp (ISO8601 format) at which the ledger transaction happened for reporting purposes.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|ledger_account_currency|string|true|none|The currency of the ledger account.|
|ledger_account_currency_exponent|integer|true|none|The currency exponent of the ledger account.|
|ledger_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ledger account that this ledger entry is associated with.|
|ledger_account_lock_version|integer \| null|true|none|Lock version of the ledger account. This can be passed when creating a ledger transaction to only succeed if no ledger transactions have posted since the given version. See our post about Designing the Ledgers API with Optimistic Locking for more details.|
|ledger_transaction_id|string|true|none|The ledger transaction that this ledger entry is associated with.|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|resulting_ledger_account_balances|object \| null|true|none|The pending, posted, and available balances for this ledger entry's ledger account. The posted balance is the sum of all posted entries on the account. The pending balance is the sum of all pending and posted entries on the account. The available balance is the posted incoming entries minus the sum of the pending and posted outgoing amounts. Please see https://docs.moderntreasury.com/docs/transaction-status-and-balances for more details.|
|status|string|true|none|Equal to the state of the ledger transaction when the ledger entry was created. One of `pending`, `posted`, or `archived`.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|credit|
|direction|debit|
|status|archived|
|status|pending|
|status|posted|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|false|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000. Can be any integer up to 36 digits.|
|client_token|string|false|none|The client token of the payment flow. This token can be used to embed a payment workflow in your client-side application.|
|counterparty_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|The ID of a counterparty associated with the payment. As part of the payment workflow an external account will be associated with this counterparty.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|currency|string|false|none|The currency of the payment.|
|direction|string|false|none|Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. Can only be `debit`. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own.|
|due_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|The due date for the flow. Can only be passed in when `effective_date_selection_enabled` is `true`.|
|effective_date_selection_enabled|boolean|false|none|When `true`, your end-user can schedule the payment `effective_date` while completing the pre-built UI.|
|existing_external_accounts_filter|string \| null|false|none|When `verified` and `external_account_collection` is `enabled`, filters the list of external accounts your end-user can select to those with a `verification_status` of `verified`.|
|external_account_collection|string|false|none|When `enabled`, your end-user can select from an existing external account when completing the flow. When `disabled`, your end-user must add new payment details when completing the flow.|
|id|string(uuid)|false|none|none|
|live_mode|boolean|false|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|object|string|false|none|none|
|originating_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|The ID of one of your organization's internal accounts.|
|payment_order_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|If present, the ID of the payment order created using this flow.|
|receiving_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|If present, the ID of the external account created using this flow.|
|selected_effective_date|string(date) \| null|false|none|This field is set after your end-user selects a payment date while completing the pre-built UI. This field is always `null` unless `effective_date_selection_enabled` is `true`.|
|status|string|false|none|The current status of the payment flow. One of `pending`, `completed`, `expired`, or `cancelled`.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounting|[accounting](#schemaaccounting)|true|none|**Deprecated.**|
|accounting_category_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting categories. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|accounting_ledger_class_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting ledger classes. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|amount|integer|true|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000 (cents). For RTP, the maximum amount allowed by the network is $10,000,000.|
|batch_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The ID of the batch in which the payment order is included. Only populated after the payment order begins processing.|
|charge_bearer|string \| null|true|none|The party that will pay the fees for the payment order. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/payments/docs/charge-bearer to understand the differences between the options.|
|counterparty_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|If the payment order is tied to a specific Counterparty, their id will appear, otherwise `null`.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|true|none|Defaults to the currency of the originating account.|
|current_hold|object \| null|true|none|If the payment order's status is `held`, this will include the hold object's data.|
|current_return|object \| null|true|none|If the payment order's status is `returned`, this will include the return object's data.|
|description|string \| null|true|none|An optional description for internal use.|
|direction|string|true|none|One of `credit`, `debit`. Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. A `credit` moves money from your account to someone else's. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own. Note that wire, rtp, and check payments will always be `credit`.|
|effective_date|string(date)|true|none|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|RFP payments require an expires_at. This value must be past the effective_date.|
|external_id|string \| null|true|none|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|foreign_exchange_contract|string \| null|true|none|If present, indicates a specific foreign exchange contract number that has been generated by your financial institution.|
|foreign_exchange_indicator|string \| null|true|none|Indicates the type of FX transfer to initiate, can be either `variable_to_fixed`, `fixed_to_variable`, or `null` if the payment order currency matches the originating account currency.|
|foreign_exchange_rate|object \| null|true|none|Associated serialized foreign exchange rate information.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|ledger_transaction_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The ID of the ledger transaction linked to the payment order.|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|nsf_protected|boolean|true|none|A boolean to determine if NSF Protection is enabled for this payment order. Note that this setting must also be turned on in your organization settings page.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|originating_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of one of your organization's internal accounts.|
|originating_account_type|string|true|none|none|
|originating_party_address|object \| null|true|none|If present, this address will override the default originating party address used on the payment order. This works across all payment types.|
|originating_party_name|string \| null|true|none|If present, this will replace your default company name on receiver's bank statement. This field can only be used for ACH payments currently. For ACH, only the first 16 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|originating_secondary_party_name|string \| null|true|none|Secondary name for the legal entity making the payment.  Can be used for e.g. check signatures where the originating party wishes to retain their company's display name but use an employee's name for the signature.|
|priority|string|true|none|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH and EFT payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH or EFT transfer, respectively. For check payments, `high` can mean an overnight check rather than standard mail.|
|process_after|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|If present, Modern Treasury will not process the payment until after this time. If `process_after` is past the cutoff for `effective_date`, `process_after` will take precedence and `effective_date` will automatically update to reflect the earliest possible sending date after `process_after`. Format is ISO8601 timestamp.|
|purpose|string \| null|true|none|For `wire`, this is usually the purpose which is transmitted via the "InstrForDbtrAgt" field in the ISO20022 file. For `eft`, this field is the 3 digit CPA Code that will be attached to the payment.|
|receiving_account|object \| null|true|none|**Deprecated.** The receiving account. Can be an `external_account` or `internal_account`.|
|receiving_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The receiving account ID. Can be an `external_account` or `internal_account`.|
|receiving_account_type|string|true|none|none|
|reconciliation_status|string|true|none|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|reference_numbers|[[payment_reference](#schemapayment_reference)]|true|none|none|
|remittance_information|string \| null|true|none|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|send_remittance_advice|boolean \| null|true|none|Send an email to the counterparty when the payment order is sent to the bank. If `null`, `send_remittance_advice` on the Counterparty is used.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|true|none|An optional descriptor which will appear in the receiver's statement. For `check` payments this field will be used as the memo line. For `ach` the maximum length is 10 characters. Note that for ACH payments, the name on your bank account will be included automatically by the bank, so you can use the characters for other useful information. For `eft` the maximum length is 15 characters.|
|status|string|true|none|The current status of the payment order.|
|subtype|[payment_order_subtype](#schemapayment_order_subtype)|true|none|An additional layer of classification for the type of payment order you are doing. This field is only used for `ach` payment orders currently. For `ach`  payment orders, the `subtype`  represents the SEC code. We currently support `CCD`, `PPD`, `IAT`, `CTX`, `WEB`, `CIE`, and `TEL`.|
|transaction_ids|[string(uuid)]|true|none|The IDs of all the transactions associated to this payment order. Usually, you will only have a single transaction ID. However, if a payment order initially results in a Return, but gets redrafted and is later successfully completed, it can have many transactions.|
|type|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|true|none|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|ultimate_originating_account|object \| null|true|none|The account to which the originating of this payment should be attributed to. Can be a `virtual_account` or `internal_account`.|
|ultimate_originating_account_id|string(uuid) \| null|true|none|The ultimate originating account ID. Can be a `virtual_account` or `internal_account`.|
|ultimate_originating_account_type|string \| null|true|none|none|
|ultimate_originating_party_identifier|string \| null|true|none|Identifier of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|ultimate_originating_party_name|string \| null|true|none|Name of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|ultimate_receiving_party_identifier|string \| null|true|none|none|
|ultimate_receiving_party_name|string \| null|true|none|none|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|vendor_attributes|object \| null|true|none|Additional vendor specific fields for this payment. Data must be represented as key-value pairs.|
|vendor_failure_reason|string \| null|true|none|This field will be populated if a vendor failure occurs. Logic shouldn't be built on its value as it is free-form.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounting|[accounting](#schemaaccounting)|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|accounting_category_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting categories. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|accounting_ledger_class_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting ledger classes. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|amount|integer|true|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000 (cents). For RTP, the maximum amount allowed by the network is $10,000,000.|
|charge_bearer|string \| null|false|none|The party that will pay the fees for the payment order. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/payments/docs/charge-bearer to understand the differences between the options.|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|none|Defaults to the currency of the originating account.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An optional description for internal use.|
|direction|string|true|none|One of `credit`, `debit`. Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. A `credit` moves money from your account to someone else's. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own. Note that wire, rtp, and check payments will always be `credit`.|
|effective_date|string(date)|false|none|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|end_to_end_id|string \| null|false|none|A unique identifier passed through to the receiving bank. Only supported for `ach` (maximum 15 characters) and `wire` (maximum 35 characters). If not provided, Modern Treasury generates one. Some banks may truncate this value or use their own identifier instead.|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|RFP payments require an expires_at. This value must be past the effective_date.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|fallback_type|string|false|none|A payment type to fallback to if the original type is not valid for the receiving account. Currently, this only supports falling back from RTP to ACH (type=rtp and fallback_type=ach)|
|foreign_exchange_contract|string \| null|false|none|If present, indicates a specific foreign exchange contract number that has been generated by your financial institution.|
|foreign_exchange_indicator|string \| null|false|none|Indicates the type of FX transfer to initiate, can be either `variable_to_fixed`, `fixed_to_variable`, or `null` if the payment order currency matches the originating account currency.|
|ledger_transaction|[ledger_transaction_create_request](#schemaledger_transaction_create_request)|false|none|Specifies a ledger transaction object that will be created with the payment order. If the ledger transaction cannot be created, then the payment order creation will fail. The resulting ledger transaction will mirror the status of the payment order.|
|ledger_transaction_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Either ledger_transaction or ledger_transaction_id can be provided. Only a pending ledger transaction can be attached upon payment order creation. Once the payment order is created, the status of the ledger transaction tracks the payment order automatically.|
|line_items|[[line_item_request](#schemaline_item_request)]|false|none|An array of line items that must sum up to the amount of the payment order.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|nsf_protected|boolean|false|none|A boolean to determine if NSF Protection is enabled for this payment order. Note that this setting must also be turned on in your organization settings page.|
|originating_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of one of your organization's internal accounts.|
|originating_party_address|object \| null|false|none|If present, this address will override the default originating party address used on the payment order. This works across all payment types.|
|originating_party_name|string \| null|false|none|If present, this will replace your default company name on receiver's bank statement. This field can only be used for ACH payments currently. For ACH, only the first 16 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|originating_secondary_party_name|string \| null|false|none|Secondary name for the legal entity making the payment.  Can be used for e.g. check signatures where the originating party wishes to retain their company's display name but use an employee's name for the signature.|
|priority|string|false|none|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH and EFT payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH or EFT transfer, respectively. For check payments, `high` can mean an overnight check rather than standard mail.|
|process_after|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|If present, Modern Treasury will not process the payment until after this time. If `process_after` is past the cutoff for `effective_date`, `process_after` will take precedence and `effective_date` will automatically update to reflect the earliest possible sending date after `process_after`. Format is ISO8601 timestamp.|
|purpose|string \| null|false|none|For `wire`, this is usually the purpose which is transmitted via the "InstrForDbtrAgt" field in the ISO20022 file. For `eft`, this field is the 3 digit CPA Code that will be attached to the payment.|
|receiving_account|object|false|none|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|receiving_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|reconciliation_status|string|false|none|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|remittance_information|string \| null|false|none|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|send_remittance_advice|boolean \| null|false|none|Send an email to the counterparty when the payment order is sent to the bank. If `null`, `send_remittance_advice` on the Counterparty is used.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|An optional descriptor which will appear in the receiver's statement. For `check` payments this field will be used as the memo line. For `ach` the maximum length is 10 characters. Note that for ACH payments, the name on your bank account will be included automatically by the bank, so you can use the characters for other useful information. For `eft` the maximum length is 15 characters.|
|subtype|[payment_order_subtype](#schemapayment_order_subtype)|false|none|An additional layer of classification for the type of payment order you are doing. This field is only used for `ach` payment orders currently. For `ach`  payment orders, the `subtype`  represents the SEC code. We currently support `CCD`, `PPD`, `IAT`, `CTX`, `WEB`, `CIE`, and `TEL`.|
|transaction_monitoring_enabled|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** A flag that determines whether a payment order should go through transaction monitoring.|
|type|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|true|none|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|ultimate_originating_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ultimate originating account ID. Can be a `virtual_account` or `internal_account`.|
|ultimate_originating_party_address|object \| null|false|none|Address of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|ultimate_originating_party_identifier|string \| null|false|none|Identifier of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|ultimate_originating_party_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|ultimate_receiving_party_identifier|string \| null|false|none|Identifier of the ultimate funds recipient.|
|ultimate_receiving_party_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the ultimate funds recipient.|
|vendor_attributes|object|false|none|Additional vendor specific fields for this payment. Data must be represented as key-value pairs.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounting|[accounting](#schemaaccounting)|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|accounting_category_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting categories. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|accounting_ledger_class_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting ledger classes. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|amount|integer|true|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000 (cents). For RTP, the maximum amount allowed by the network is $10,000,000.|
|charge_bearer|string \| null|false|none|The party that will pay the fees for the payment order. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/payments/docs/charge-bearer to understand the differences between the options.|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|none|Defaults to the currency of the originating account.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An optional description for internal use.|
|direction|string|true|none|One of `credit`, `debit`. Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. A `credit` moves money from your account to someone else's. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own. Note that wire, rtp, and check payments will always be `credit`.|
|documents|[[payment_order_document_create_request](#schemapayment_order_document_create_request)]|false|none|An array of documents to be attached to the payment order. Note that if you attach documents, the request's content type must be `multipart/form-data`.|
|effective_date|string(date)|false|none|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|end_to_end_id|string \| null|false|none|A unique identifier passed through to the receiving bank. Only supported for `ach` (maximum 15 characters) and `wire` (maximum 35 characters). If not provided, Modern Treasury generates one. Some banks may truncate this value or use their own identifier instead.|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|RFP payments require an expires_at. This value must be past the effective_date.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|fallback_type|string|false|none|A payment type to fallback to if the original type is not valid for the receiving account. Currently, this only supports falling back from RTP to ACH (type=rtp and fallback_type=ach)|
|foreign_exchange_contract|string \| null|false|none|If present, indicates a specific foreign exchange contract number that has been generated by your financial institution.|
|foreign_exchange_indicator|string \| null|false|none|Indicates the type of FX transfer to initiate, can be either `variable_to_fixed`, `fixed_to_variable`, or `null` if the payment order currency matches the originating account currency.|
|ledger_transaction|[ledger_transaction_create_request](#schemaledger_transaction_create_request)|false|none|Specifies a ledger transaction object that will be created with the payment order. If the ledger transaction cannot be created, then the payment order creation will fail. The resulting ledger transaction will mirror the status of the payment order.|
|ledger_transaction_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Either ledger_transaction or ledger_transaction_id can be provided. Only a pending ledger transaction can be attached upon payment order creation. Once the payment order is created, the status of the ledger transaction tracks the payment order automatically.|
|line_items|[[line_item_request](#schemaline_item_request)]|false|none|An array of line items that must sum up to the amount of the payment order.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|nsf_protected|boolean|false|none|A boolean to determine if NSF Protection is enabled for this payment order. Note that this setting must also be turned on in your organization settings page.|
|originating_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of one of your organization's internal accounts.|
|originating_party_address|object \| null|false|none|If present, this address will override the default originating party address used on the payment order. This works across all payment types.|
|originating_party_name|string \| null|false|none|If present, this will replace your default company name on receiver's bank statement. This field can only be used for ACH payments currently. For ACH, only the first 16 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|originating_secondary_party_name|string \| null|false|none|Secondary name for the legal entity making the payment.  Can be used for e.g. check signatures where the originating party wishes to retain their company's display name but use an employee's name for the signature.|
|priority|string|false|none|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH and EFT payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH or EFT transfer, respectively. For check payments, `high` can mean an overnight check rather than standard mail.|
|process_after|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|If present, Modern Treasury will not process the payment until after this time. If `process_after` is past the cutoff for `effective_date`, `process_after` will take precedence and `effective_date` will automatically update to reflect the earliest possible sending date after `process_after`. Format is ISO8601 timestamp.|
|purpose|string \| null|false|none|For `wire`, this is usually the purpose which is transmitted via the "InstrForDbtrAgt" field in the ISO20022 file. For `eft`, this field is the 3 digit CPA Code that will be attached to the payment.|
|receiving_account|object|false|none|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|receiving_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|reconciliation_status|string|false|none|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|remittance_information|string \| null|false|none|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|send_remittance_advice|boolean \| null|false|none|Send an email to the counterparty when the payment order is sent to the bank. If `null`, `send_remittance_advice` on the Counterparty is used.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|An optional descriptor which will appear in the receiver's statement. For `check` payments this field will be used as the memo line. For `ach` the maximum length is 10 characters. Note that for ACH payments, the name on your bank account will be included automatically by the bank, so you can use the characters for other useful information. For `eft` the maximum length is 15 characters.|
|subtype|[payment_order_subtype](#schemapayment_order_subtype)|false|none|An additional layer of classification for the type of payment order you are doing. This field is only used for `ach` payment orders currently. For `ach`  payment orders, the `subtype`  represents the SEC code. We currently support `CCD`, `PPD`, `IAT`, `CTX`, `WEB`, `CIE`, and `TEL`.|
|transaction_monitoring_enabled|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** A flag that determines whether a payment order should go through transaction monitoring.|
|type|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|true|none|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|ultimate_originating_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ultimate originating account ID. Can be a `virtual_account` or `internal_account`.|
|ultimate_originating_party_address|object \| null|false|none|Address of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|ultimate_originating_party_identifier|string \| null|false|none|Identifier of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|ultimate_originating_party_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the ultimate originator of the payment order.|
|ultimate_receiving_party_identifier|string \| null|false|none|Identifier of the ultimate funds recipient.|
|ultimate_receiving_party_name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the ultimate funds recipient.|
|vendor_attributes|object|false|none|Additional vendor specific fields for this payment. Data must be represented as key-value pairs.|

<h2 id="tocS_payment_order_subtype">payment_order_subtype</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapayment_order_subtype"></a>
<a id="schema_payment_order_subtype"></a>
<a id="tocSpayment_order_subtype"></a>
<a id="tocspayment_order_subtype"></a>

```json
"0C"
```

An additional layer of classification for the type of payment order you are doing. This field is only used for `ach` payment orders currently. For `ach`  payment orders, the `subtype`  represents the SEC code. We currently support `CCD`, `PPD`, `IAT`, `CTX`, `WEB`, `CIE`, and `TEL`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accounting|[accounting](#schemaaccounting)|false|none|**Deprecated.**|
|accounting_category_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting categories. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|accounting_ledger_class_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** The ID of one of your accounting ledger classes. Note that these will only be accessible if your accounting system has been connected.|
|amount|integer|false|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000 (cents). For RTP, the maximum amount allowed by the network is $10,000,000.|
|charge_bearer|string \| null|false|none|The party that will pay the fees for the payment order. See https://docs.moderntreasury.com/payments/docs/charge-bearer to understand the differences between the options.|
|counterparty_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Required when receiving_account_id is passed the ID of an external account.|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|none|Defaults to the currency of the originating account.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An optional description for internal use.|
|direction|string|false|none|One of `credit`, `debit`. Describes the direction money is flowing in the transaction. A `credit` moves money from your account to someone else's. A `debit` pulls money from someone else's account to your own. Note that wire, rtp, and check payments will always be `credit`.|
|effective_date|string(date)|false|none|Date transactions are to be posted to the participants' account. Defaults to the current business day or the next business day if the current day is a bank holiday or weekend. Format: yyyy-mm-dd.|
|end_to_end_id|string \| null|false|none|A unique identifier passed through to the receiving bank. Only supported for `ach` (maximum 15 characters) and `wire` (maximum 35 characters). If not provided, Modern Treasury generates one. Some banks may truncate this value or use their own identifier instead.|
|expires_at|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|RFP payments require an expires_at. This value must be past the effective_date.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|An optional user-defined 180 character unique identifier.|
|fallback_type|string|false|none|A payment type to fallback to if the original type is not valid for the receiving account. Currently, this only supports falling back from RTP to ACH (type=rtp and fallback_type=ach)|
|foreign_exchange_contract|string \| null|false|none|If present, indicates a specific foreign exchange contract number that has been generated by your financial institution.|
|foreign_exchange_indicator|string \| null|false|none|Indicates the type of FX transfer to initiate, can be either `variable_to_fixed`, `fixed_to_variable`, or `null` if the payment order currency matches the originating account currency.|
|line_items|[[line_item_request](#schemaline_item_request)]|false|none|An array of line items that must sum up to the amount of the payment order.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|nsf_protected|boolean|false|none|A boolean to determine if NSF Protection is enabled for this payment order. Note that this setting must also be turned on in your organization settings page.|
|originating_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ID of one of your organization's internal accounts.|
|originating_party_address|object \| null|false|none|If present, this address will override the default originating party address used on the payment order. This works across all payment types.|
|originating_party_name|string \| null|false|none|If present, this will replace your default company name on receiver's bank statement. This field can only be used for ACH payments currently. For ACH, only the first 16 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|originating_secondary_party_name|string \| null|false|none|Secondary name for the legal entity making the payment.  Can be used for e.g. check signatures where the originating party wishes to retain their company's display name but use an employee's name for the signature.|
|priority|string|false|none|Either `normal` or `high`. For ACH and EFT payments, `high` represents a same-day ACH or EFT transfer, respectively. For check payments, `high` can mean an overnight check rather than standard mail.|
|process_after|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|If present, Modern Treasury will not process the payment until after this time. If `process_after` is past the cutoff for `effective_date`, `process_after` will take precedence and `effective_date` will automatically update to reflect the earliest possible sending date after `process_after`. Format is ISO8601 timestamp.|
|purpose|string \| null|false|none|For `wire`, this is usually the purpose which is transmitted via the "InstrForDbtrAgt" field in the ISO20022 file. For `eft`, this field is the 3 digit CPA Code that will be attached to the payment.|
|receiving_account|object|false|none|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|receiving_account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Either `receiving_account` or `receiving_account_id` must be present. When using `receiving_account_id`, you may pass the id of an external account or an internal account.|
|reconciliation_status|string|false|none|One of `unreconciled`, `tentatively_reconciled` or `reconciled`.|
|remittance_information|string \| null|false|none|For `ach`, this field will be passed through on an addenda record. For `wire` payments the field will be passed through as the "Originator to Beneficiary Information", also known as OBI or Fedwire tag 6000.|
|send_remittance_advice|boolean \| null|false|none|Send an email to the counterparty when the payment order is sent to the bank. If `null`, `send_remittance_advice` on the Counterparty is used.|
|statement_descriptor|string \| null|false|none|An optional descriptor which will appear in the receiver's statement. For `check` payments this field will be used as the memo line. For `ach` the maximum length is 10 characters. Note that for ACH payments, the name on your bank account will be included automatically by the bank, so you can use the characters for other useful information. For `eft` the maximum length is 15 characters.|
|status|string|false|none|To cancel a payment order, use `cancelled`. To redraft a returned payment order, use `approved`. To undo approval on a denied or approved payment order, use `needs_approval`.|
|subtype|[payment_order_subtype](#schemapayment_order_subtype)|false|none|An additional layer of classification for the type of payment order you are doing. This field is only used for `ach` payment orders currently. For `ach`  payment orders, the `subtype`  represents the SEC code. We currently support `CCD`, `PPD`, `IAT`, `CTX`, `WEB`, `CIE`, and `TEL`.|
|type|[payment_order_type](#schemapayment_order_type)|false|none|One of `ach`, `se_bankgirot`, `eft`, `wire`, `check`, `book`, `rtp`, `sepa`, `bacs`, `au_becs`, `neft`, `nics`, `nz_national_clearing_code`, `sic`, `zengin`.|
|ultimate_originating_party_identifier|string \| null|false|none|This represents the identifier by which the person is known to the receiver when using the CIE subtype for ACH payments. Only the first 22 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|ultimate_originating_party_name|string \| null|false|none|This represents the name of the person that the payment is on behalf of when using the CIE subtype for ACH payments. Only the first 15 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|ultimate_receiving_party_identifier|string \| null|false|none|This represents the name of the merchant that the payment is being sent to when using the CIE subtype for ACH payments. Only the first 22 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|
|ultimate_receiving_party_name|string \| null|false|none|This represents the identifier by which the merchant is known to the person initiating an ACH payment with CIE subtype. Only the first 15 characters of this string will be used. Any additional characters will be truncated.|

  },

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount_lower_bound|integer|true|none|The lowest amount this expected payment may be equal to. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|amount_upper_bound|integer|true|none|The highest amount this expected payment may be equal to. Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|counterparty_id|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|The ID of the counterparty you expect for this payment|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|false|none|Must conform to ISO 4217. Defaults to the currency of the internal account|
|custom_identifiers|object \| null|false|none|A hash of custom identifiers for this payment|
|date_lower_bound|string(date) \| null|false|none|The earliest date the payment may come in. Format is yyyy-mm-dd|
|date_upper_bound|string(date) \| null|false|none|The latest date the payment may come in. Format is yyyy-mm-dd|
|direction|string|true|none|One of credit or debit. When you are receiving money, use credit. When you are being charged, use debit.|
|internal_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of the Internal Account for the expected payment|
|type|string \| null|false|none|One of ach, au_becs, bacs, book, check, eft, rtp, sepa, wire|

<h2 id="tocS_transaction">transaction</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransaction"></a>
<a id="schema_transaction"></a>
<a id="tocStransaction"></a>
<a id="tocstransaction"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "amount_string": "string",
  "as_of_date": "1970-01-01",
  "as_of_time": "00:00:00Z",
  "as_of_timezone": "string",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "currency": "AED",
  "custom_identifiers": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "details": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "direction": "string",
  "discarded_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "foreign_exchange_rate": {
    "base_amount": 0,
    "base_currency": "AED",
    "exponent": 0,
    "rate_string": "string",
    "target_amount": 0,
    "target_currency": "AED",
    "value": 0
  },
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "live_mode": true,
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "object": "string",
  "posted": true,
  "reconciled": true,
  "type": "ach",
  "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "vendor_code": "string",
  "vendor_code_type": "bai2",
  "vendor_customer_id": "string",
  "vendor_description": "string",
  "vendor_id": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|amount_string|string|true|none|The amount of the transaction as a string, preserving full precision for values that may exceed safe integer limits in some languages.|
|as_of_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date on which the transaction occurred.|
|as_of_time|string(time) \| null|true|none|The time on which the transaction occurred. Depending on the granularity of the timestamp information received from the bank, it may be `null`.|
|as_of_timezone|string \| null|true|none|The timezone in which the `as_of_time` is represented. Can be `null` if the bank does not provide timezone info.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|currency|[currency](#schemacurrency)|true|none|Currency that this transaction is denominated in.|
|custom_identifiers|object|true|none|An object containing key-value pairs, each with a custom identifier as the key and a string value.|
|details|object|false|none|This field contains additional information that the bank provided about the transaction. This is structured data. Some of the data in here might overlap with what is in the `vendor_description`. For example, the OBI could be a part of the vendor description, and it would also be included in here. The attributes that are passed through the details field will vary based on your banking partner. Currently, the following keys may be in the details object: `originator_name`, `originator_to_beneficiary_information`.|
|direction|string|true|none|Either `credit` or `debit`.|
|discarded_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|none|
|foreign_exchange_rate|object \| null|true|none|Associated serialized foreign exchange rate information.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|internal_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of the relevant Internal Account.|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|posted|boolean|true|none|This field will be `true` if the transaction has posted to the account.|
|reconciled|boolean|true|none|This field will be `true` if a transaction is reconciled by the Modern Treasury system. This means that it has transaction line items that sum up to the transaction's amount.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the transaction. Examples could be `card, `ach`, `wire`, `check`, `rtp`, or `book`.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|vendor_code|string \| null|true|none|When applicable, the bank-given code that determines the transaction's category. For most banks this is the BAI2/BTRS transaction code.|

<h2 id="tocS_transaction_create_request">transaction_create_request</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematransaction_create_request"></a>
<a id="schema_transaction_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocStransaction_create_request"></a>
<a id="tocstransaction_create_request"></a>

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "amount_string": "string",
  "as_of_date": "1970-01-01",
  "direction": "string",
  "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "metadata": {
    "foo": "bar",
    "key": "value",
    "modern": "treasury"
  },
  "posted": true,
  "type": "ach",
  "vendor_code": "string",
  "vendor_code_type": "string",
  "vendor_customer_id": "string",
  "vendor_description": "string"
}
```

At least one of "amount" or "amount_string" is required.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|false|none|Value in specified currency's smallest unit. e.g. $10 would be represented as 1000.|
|amount_string|string|false|none|The transaction amount as a string, preserving full precision for values that may exceed safe integer limits in some languages.|
|as_of_date|string(date) \| null|true|none|The date on which the transaction occurred.|
|direction|string|true|none|Either `credit` or `debit`.|
|internal_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of the relevant Internal Account.|
|metadata|object|false|none|Additional data represented as key-value pairs. Both the key and value must be strings.|
|posted|boolean|false|none|This field will be `true` if the transaction has posted to the account.|
|type|string \| null|false|none|The type of the transaction. Examples could be `card, `ach`, `wire`, `check`, `rtp`, or `book`.|
|vendor_code|string \| null|true|none|When applicable, the bank-given code that determines the transaction's category. For most banks this is the BAI2/BTRS transaction code.|
|vendor_code_type|string \| null|true|none|The type of `vendor_code` being reported. Can be one of `bai2`, `bankprov`, `bnk_dev`, `cleartouch`, `currencycloud`, `cross_river`, `dwolla`, `evolve`, `goldman_sachs`, `iso20022`, `jpmc`, `mx`, `silvergate`, `swift`, `us_bank`, or others.|
|vendor_customer_id|string \| null|false|none|An identifier given to this transaction by the bank, often `null`.|
|vendor_description|string \| null|false|none|The transaction detail text that often appears in on your bank statement and in your banking portal.|

```json
{
  "amount": 0,
  "counterparty_id": "string",

  "description": "string",
  "discarded_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "expected_payment_id": "string",
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "live_mode": true,
  "object": "string",
  "reconcilable": true,
  "reconciliation_group_id": "string",
  "transactable_id": "string",
  "transactable_type": "incoming_payment_detail",
  "transaction_id": "string",
  "type": "originating",
  "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|amount|integer|true|none|If a matching object exists in Modern Treasury, `amount` will be populated. Value in specified currency's smallest unit (taken from parent Transaction).|
|counterparty_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID for the counterparty for this transaction line item.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|
|description|string|true|none|If no matching object is found, `description` will be a free-form text field describing the line item. This field may contain personally identifiable information (PII) and is not included in API responses by default. Learn more about changing your settings at https://docs.moderntreasury.com/reference/personally-identifiable-information.|
|discarded_at|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|none|
|expected_payment_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the reconciled Expected Payment, otherwise `null`.|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|none|
|live_mode|boolean|true|none|This field will be true if this object exists in the live environment, or false if it exists in the test environment.|
|object|string|true|none|none|
|reconcilable|boolean|true|none|Describes whether this line item should be counted towards the corresponding transaction’s reconciliation.|
|reconciliation_group_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the reconciliation group this line item belongs to, otherwise `null`.|
|transactable_id|string \| null|true|none|If a matching object exists in Modern Treasury, the ID will be populated here, otherwise `null`.|
|transactable_type|string \| null|true|none|If a matching object exists in Modern Treasury, the type will be populated here, otherwise `null`.|
|transaction_id|string|true|none|The ID of the parent transaction.|
|type|string|true|none|Indicates whether the line item is `originating` or `receiving` (see https://www.moderntreasury.com/journal/beginners-guide-to-ach for more).|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_virtual_account_setting_create_request">virtual_account_setting_create_request</h2>

```json
{
  "allocation_identifier": "string",
  "allocation_length": 0,
  "allocation_range_end": "string",
  "allocation_range_start": "string",
  "allocation_type": "string",
  "external_id": "string",
  "generated_allocation_identifier_length": 0,
  "internal_account_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allocation_identifier|string \| null|false|none|The prefix, suffix, or bank-assigned identifier for the virtual account numbers.|
|allocation_length|integer \| null|false|none|The total length of generated virtual account numbers.|
|allocation_range_end|string \| null|false|none|The inclusive end of the virtual account number range.|
|allocation_range_start|string \| null|false|none|The inclusive start of the virtual account number range.|
|allocation_type|string|true|none|The method used to allocate virtual account numbers.|
|external_id|string \| null|false|none|A user-defined identifier for the virtual account setting.|
|generated_allocation_identifier_length|integer \| null|false|none|The length of a generated virtual account setting prefix.|
|internal_account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The ID of the internal account for the virtual account setting.|
